sentences.zh: 石虎

translations.literal: Shi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong, known as Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: ，季龍親耕藉田于其桑梓苑，其妻杜氏祠先蠶於近郊，遂如襄國謁勒墓。

translations.literal: Jilong personally plowed the ritual field at his Mulberry-and-Catalpa Park; his wife Lady Du offered sacrifice to the First Silkworm beyond the suburbs; then he proceeded to Xiangguo to visit Le's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong plowed the ceremonial field in his private Mulberry Park; Lady Du sacrificed to the silkworm goddess in the near suburbs; then he rode to Xiangguo to bow at Shi Le's tomb.

sentences.zh: 以中書監石寧為征西將軍，率并、司州兵二餘人為麻秋等後繼。

translations.literal: He appointed Palace Secretariat Supervisor Shi Ning as General Who Conquers the West and led Bing- and Si-province troops numbering more than twenty thousand to serve as rear support for Ma Qiu and others.
translations.idiomatic: He named Shi Ning of the secretariat general for the western campaign and sent upward of twenty thousand soldiers from Bing and Si provinces to reinforce Ma Qiu's column.

sentences.zh: 張重華將宋秦等率戶二萬來降。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua's generals Song Qin and others led twenty thousand households to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qin and other officers under Zhang Chonghua marched twenty thousand households over to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 河湟間氐羌十餘萬落與張璩相首尾，麻秋憚之，不進。

translations.literal: Between the He and Huang more than one hundred thousand Di and Qiang households linked head to tail with Zhang Qu; Ma Qiu feared them and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred thousand Di and Qiang lodges along the He-Huang corridor coordinated with Zhang Qu; Ma Qiu dared not push forward against them.

sentences.zh: 重華金城太守張沖又以郡降石寧。

translations.literal: Chonghua's Jincheng prefect Zhang Chong also surrendered the commandery to Shi Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, Jincheng governor under Zhang Chonghua, likewise handed his district to Shi Ning.

sentences.zh: 麻秋尋次曲柳，劉甯、王擢進攻晉興武街。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu soon encamped at Qu Liu; Liu Ning and Wang Zhuo advanced to attack Jinxing and Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu halted at Qu Liu while Liu Ning and Wang Zhuo pressed the attack on Jinxing and Wujie.

sentences.zh: 重華將楊康等與甯戰于沙阜，寧敗績，乃引還金城。

translations.literal: Chonghua's generals Yang Kang and others fought Ning at Sandy Mound; Ning suffered rout; then he led the army back to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kang and his men met Shi Ning on Sandy Hill, broke his line, and drove him back to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 王擢克武街，執重華護軍曹權、胡宣，徙七千餘戶於雍州。

translations.literal: Wang Zhuo took Wujie, captured Chonghua's garrison commanders Cao Quan and Hu Xuan, and relocated more than seven thousand households to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo seized Wujie, took garrison officers Cao Quan and Hu Xuan prisoner, and deported over seven thousand households into Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 季龍又以孫伏都為征西將軍，與麻秋率步騎三萬長驅濟河，且城長最。

translations.literal: Jilong also appointed Sun Fudu as General Who Conquers the West; together with Ma Qiu he led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry in a long drive across the River and moreover fortified Changzui.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu named Sun Fudu western-expedition general; with Ma Qiu he took thirty thousand horse and foot straight across the Yellow River and threw up a fortress at Changzui.

sentences.zh: 重華大懼，遣將謝艾逆擊，敗之，秋退歸金城。

translations.literal: Chonghua was greatly afraid, sent general Xie Ai to strike them in reverse, defeated them, and Qiu withdrew and returned to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua panicked and sent Xie Ai to counterattack; Ma Qiu was routed and fell back to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 勒及季龍並貪而無禮，既王有十州之地，金帛珠玉及外國珍奇異貨不可勝紀，而猶以為不足，曩代帝王及先賢陵墓靡不發掘，而取其寶貨焉。

translations.literal: Le and Jilong alike were greedy and without propriety; once they had kingly rule over ten provinces' territory, gold, silk, pearls, jade, and foreign rare and marvelous goods could not all be recorded, yet they still deemed it insufficient; former dynasties' emperors and worthies' tombs there was none they did not open, taking their treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Shi Jilong were insatiable and shameless: though ten provinces poured gold, gems, and exotic tribute into their treasuries, they still wanted more, and they rifled every royal and sage tomb they could find for burial wealth.

sentences.zh: 邯鄲城西石子堈上有趙簡子墓，至是季龍令發之，初得炭深丈餘，次得木板厚一尺，積板厚八尺，乃及泉，其水清冷非常，作絞車以牛皮囊汲之，月餘而水不盡，不可發而止。

translations.literal: On the stone mound west of Handan city stood the tomb of Zhao Jianzi; at this point Jilong ordered it opened. At first they obtained charcoal more than one zhang deep, next wooden planks one chi thick; the stacked planks reached eight chi thick before they reached the spring; its water was unusually clear and cold. They built a winch and drew it with ox-hide bags; after more than a month the water did not end, so they could not continue the opening and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: West of Handan lay Zhao Jianzi's tomb on Stone Mound Hill; Shi Hu had it broken open. They dug through charcoal, then a yard of planking, then eight feet of layered boards, until they struck an icy spring. Winches and leather buckets ran for a month without draining it, so the dig had to be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又使掘秦始皇塚，取銅柱鑄以為器。

translations.literal: He also had them dig the tomb of the First Emperor of Qin, took the bronze pillars, and cast them into vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened Qin Shihuang's mausoleum, stripped its bronze pillars, and melted them down for ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 時沙門吳進言于季龍曰：「胡運將衰，晉當復興，宜若役晉人以厭其氣。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Wu Jin spoke to Jilong, saying: "The fortune of the Hu is about to wane; Jin is about to revive; you ought to employ Jin people in corvée to suppress their qi."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Wu Jin told Shi Hu, "The Hu star is falling and Jin will rise again—conscript ethnic Han laborers to break their ascendancy."

sentences.zh: 」季龍於是使尚書張群發近郡男女十六萬，車十萬乘，運土築華林苑及長牆於鄴北，廣長數十里。

translations.literal: Jilong thereupon ordered Masters-of-Writing Zhang Qun to levy one hundred sixty thousand men and women of the near commanderies, one hundred thousand carts, to transport earth and build the Hualin Park and a long wall north of Ye, breadth and length several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu then had Zhang Qun draft a hundred and sixty thousand civilians from neighboring districts and a hundred thousand carts to haul earth for Hualin Park and a miles-long rampart north of Ye.

sentences.zh: 趙攬、申鐘、石璞等上疏陳天文錯亂，蒼生凋弊，及因引見，又面諫，辭旨甚切。

translations.literal: Zhao Lan, Shen Zhong, Shi Pu, and others submitted memorials setting forth that celestial patterns were disordered and the common people were wasted and exhausted; when they were summoned for audience they remonstrated face to face, their words extremely pointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lan, Shen Zhong, and Shi Pu petitioned about erratic omens and a broken populace; at audience they spoke bluntly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 季龍大怒曰：「牆朝戌夕沒，吾無恨矣。

translations.literal: Jilong raged greatly and said: "If the wall stands by morning and is gone by evening, We shall still have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu thundered that even if the wall rose at dawn and sank by dusk he would not repent—he would have the work done at any human cost.

sentences.zh: 」乃促張群以燭夜作。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pressed Zhang Qun to labor by candlelight through the nights.
translations.idiomatic: He drove Zhang Qun's gangs to work by torchlight night after night.

sentences.zh: 起三觀、四門，三門通漳水，皆為鐵扉。

translations.literal: They raised three belvederes and four gates; three gates communicated with the Zhang River; all had iron doors.
translations.idiomatic: They raised three towers and four gates, three of them opening onto the Zhang with iron doors.

sentences.zh: 暴風大雨，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Violent wind and great rain; those who died numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: A howling storm followed, killing tens of thousands of laborers.

sentences.zh: 揚州送黃鵠雛五，頸長一丈，聲聞十餘里，泛之于玄武池。

translations.literal: Yangzhou presented five yellow-swan chicks whose necks were one zhang long; their cries were heard more than ten li; they were set afloat on the Xuanwu Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou sent five cygnets with yard-long necks whose calls carried ten li; they were released on the Xuanwu Pool.

sentences.zh: 郡國前後送蒼麟十六，白鹿七，季龍命司虞張曷柱調之，以駕芝蓋，列於充庭之乘。

translations.literal: The commanderies before and after presented sixteen blue unicorns and seven white deer; Jilong ordered the herds intendant Zhang Hezhu to train them, to draw fungus-pattern canopies, arrayed among the court chariots filling the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Districts sent sixteen blue deer and seven white stags; Shi Hu had Zhang Hezhu break them to the rein for fungus-canopied state carriages ranked in the forecourt.

sentences.zh: 鑿北城，引水于華林園。

translations.literal: They cut through the north city wall and led water into the Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: They breached the north wall to feed the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 城崩，壓死者百餘人。

translations.literal: The wall collapsed; those crushed to death exceeded one hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: The breach collapsed and buried more than a hundred workers.

sentences.zh: 命石宣祈於山川，因而遊獵，乘大輅，羽葆、華蓋，建天子旌旗，十有六軍，戎卒十八萬，出自金明門。

translations.literal: He ordered Shi Xuan to pray at mountains and rivers, and thereby to roam and hunt; riding the great chariot with feathered canopy and flowered parasol, he set up Son-of-Heaven banners and flags, sixteen armies, one hundred eighty thousand field troops, and went out through the Golden Bright Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shi Xuan to sacrifice along the rivers, then turned the outing into a hunt: the heir rode the state chariot under feather fans and imperial banners with sixteen hosts and a hundred and eighty thousand men out the Golden Bright Gate.

sentences.zh: 季龍從其後宮升陵霄觀望之，笑曰：「我家父子如是，自非天崩地陷，當復何愁，但抱子弄孫日為樂耳！

translations.literal: Jilong ascended the Lingxiao Belvedere from his rear palace to watch them and laughed, saying: "With father and son of Our house like this, unless heaven collapses and earth sinks, what again is there to worry about? We need only cradle sons and dandle grandsons and take daily pleasure!"
translations.idiomatic: From the Lingxiao tower Shi Hu watched his heir's pageant and laughed, "While we rule like this, unless sky and earth cave in, what is left to fear? I need only rock grandsons on my knee and enjoy each day!"

sentences.zh: 」宣既馳逐無厭，所在陳列行宮，四面各以百里為度，驅圍禽獸，皆幕集其所。

translations.literal: " Once Xuan had galloped and chased without satiety, wherever he went he set out traveling palaces, on each of the four sides taking one hundred li as the measure; he drove and encircled birds and beasts, all with tents massed where they were.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan hunted without restraint, pitching field palaces on a hundred-li square, driving game into corrals thick with tents.

sentences.zh: 文武跪立，圍守重行，烽炬星羅，光燭如晝，命勁騎百餘馳射其中。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials knelt standing; the encircling guard stood in multiple ranks; beacon torches were spread like stars; the light shone as if daytime; he ordered more than one hundred picked horsemen to gallop and shoot within it.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers knelt in ranks while ring after ring of guards and torches turned night to noon; a hundred picked riders galloped inside, loosing arrows at the penned beasts.

sentences.zh: 宣與嬖姬顯德美人乘輦觀之，嬉娛忘反，獸殫乃止。

translations.literal: Xuan together with his favored concubines Xiande and the Meiren rode a litter to watch it, frolicked and forgot to return, and only when the beasts were exhausted did they stop.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan and his favorite Xiande rode a palanquin to watch, lost themselves in sport until the quarry was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 其有禽獸奔逸，當之者坐，有爵者奪馬步驅一日，無爵者鞭之一百。

translations.literal: If there were birds and beasts that broke away in flight, those who stood in their path were held guilty; those with noble rank had their horses taken and were made to walk and drive a cart one day; those without noble rank were whipped one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Any beast that broke the ring made whoever blocked its path liable: titled men lost their mounts and had to haul carts on foot for a day; commoners took a hundred lashes.

sentences.zh: 峻制嚴刑，文武戰慄，士卒饑凍而死者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: Harsh regulations and severe punishments; civil and military trembled; soldiers who died of hunger and cold exceeded ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Draconian edicts kept every official shaking while more than ten thousand troopers froze or starved on the hunt.

sentences.zh: 宣弓馬衣食皆號為禦，有亂其間者，以冒禁罪罪之。

translations.literal: Xuan's bows, horses, clothing, and food were all labeled "imperial"; whoever disturbed among them was punished with the crime of violating prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Everything from Shi Xuan's tack to his rations was stamped "imperial"; touch it and you were charged with lèse-majesté.

sentences.zh: 所過三州十五郡，資儲靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: Of the three provinces and fifteen commanderies they passed through, supplies and stores left not a remnant.
translations.idiomatic: Three provinces and fifteen commanderies were stripped bare as he passed.

sentences.zh: 季龍復命石韜亦如之，出自并州，游于秦、晉。

translations.literal: Jilong again ordered Shi Tao to do likewise; he went out from Bingzhou and roamed in Qin and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu then told Shi Tao to mount the same spectacle out of Bingzhou across Qin and Jin.

sentences.zh: 宣素惡韜寵，是行也，嫉之彌甚。

translations.literal: Xuan had always hated Tao's favor; on this expedition his jealousy grew still more severe.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan had long resented Shi Tao's favor at court, and this tour only deepened his envy.

sentences.zh: 宦者趙生得幸于宣而無寵於韜，微勸宣除之，於是相圖之計起矣。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhao Sheng had won favor with Xuan but had no favor with Tao; he subtly urged Xuan to remove him; thereupon plans to destroy each other arose.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhao Sheng, Shi Xuan's creature but not Shi Tao's, quietly urged fratricide—and the brothers began plotting each other's ruin.

sentences.zh: 麻秋又襲張重華將張瑁於河、陝，敗之，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu again raided Zhang Chonghua's general Zhang Mao at He and Shan, defeated him, and beheaded more than three thousand levels.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu struck Zhang Mao between the Yellow River and the Shan passes, routed him, and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 枹罕護軍李逵率眾七千降于季龍。

translations.literal: Bohan garrison commander Li Kui led a host of seven thousand to surrender to Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, warden of Fuhan, brought seven thousand men over to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 自河已南，氐、羌皆降。

translations.literal: South of the River the Di and Qiang all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: South of the great river every Di and Qiang band submitted.

sentences.zh: 石韜起堂于太尉府，號曰宣光殿，梁長九丈。

translations.literal: Shi Tao raised a hall in the grand marshal's office, titled it the Hall of Shining Light; its beam was nine zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao built a reception hall in the grand marshal's compound and named it Xuanguang; its ridgebeam spanned nine zhang.

sentences.zh: 宣視而大怒，斬匠，截梁而去。

translations.literal: When Xuan saw it he was greatly enraged; he executed the craftsmen, cut the beam, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan took one look, executed the builders, hacked the beam out, and stalked off.

sentences.zh: 韜怒，增之十丈。

translations.literal: Tao was angry and increased it to ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao rebuilt it higher, stretching the beam to ten zhang.

sentences.zh: 宣聞之，恚甚，謂所幸楊柸、牟成曰：「韜凶豎勃逆，敢違我如是！

translations.literal: When Xuan heard of it he was furious in the extreme and said to those he favored, Yang Pei and Mou Cheng: "That vicious boy Tao rebels and dares defy Us like this!
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xuan heard, he raged to his favorites Yang Pei and Mou Cheng, "That whelp Shi Tao dares flout me like a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 汝能殺之者，吾入西宮，當盡以韜之國邑分封汝等。

translations.literal: If you can kill him, when We enter the West Palace We shall entirely divide Tao's state and towns among you as enfeoffments."
translations.idiomatic: "Kill him for me," he swore, "and once I hold the western palace I will carve up Shi Tao's fiefs among you."

sentences.zh: 韜既死，主上必親臨喪，因行大事，蔑不濟矣。

translations.literal: Once Tao is dead, the sovereign is sure to attend the mourning in person; by carrying out a great coup then, nothing will fail."
translations.idiomatic: "When he falls, the old man will come to the bier in person—strike then and nothing can go wrong."

sentences.zh: 」柸等許諾。

translations.literal: " Pei and the others promised.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pei and the rest swore to do it.

sentences.zh: 時東南有黃黑雲，大如數畝，稍分為三，狀若匹布，東西經天，色黑而青，酉時貫日，日沒後分為七道，每相去數十丈，間有白雲如魚鱗，子時乃滅。

translations.literal: At that time in the southeast there was a yellow-black cloud as large as several mu of land; it gradually split into three, shaped like a bolt of cloth, stretching east-west across the sky; its color was black yet greenish; at the rooster hour it pierced the sun; after the sun set it split into seven paths, each several tens of zhang apart; between them were white clouds like fish scales; at the midnight hour it then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow-black cloud several acres wide split into three bands like drapery across the southeast sky, black-green at dusk punching the disk of the sun; after nightfall it forked into seven lanes scored with fish-scale clouds until midnight, when it faded.

sentences.zh: 韜素解天文，見而惡之，顧謂左右曰：「此變不小，當有刺客起于京師，不知誰定當之？

translations.literal: Tao by nature understood astronomy; when he saw it he hated the omen and, turning to those at his side, said: "This portent is not small; there ought to be an assassin arising in the capital—who is fated to receive it?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao, who read the skies, muttered to his staff, "This is no small omen—an assassin is coming inside the walls, but who will pay the price?"

sentences.zh: 」是夜，韜宴其僚屬于東明觀，樂奏，酒酣，愀然長歎曰：「人居世無常，別易會難。

translations.literal: " That night Tao feasted his staff and subordinates at the Eastern Brightness Belvedere; when the music played and the wine was warm, he looked grim and sighed long, saying: "Human dwelling in the world is impermanent; parting is easy, meeting hard.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he feasted his officers at the Eastern Brightness tower; halfway through the wine he sighed, "Life is fleeting—parting comes easier than reunion."

sentences.zh: 各付一杯，開意為吾飲，令必醉。

translations.literal: Each take one cup; open your hearts and drink for Us; We order you must get drunk.
translations.idiomatic: "Take a cup each and drink your hearts out—I mean you all drunk tonight."

sentences.zh: 知後會復何期而不飲乎！

translations.literal: Knowing what later meeting again will be like, how can you not drink!"
translations.idiomatic: "Who knows if we shall meet again—how can you refuse the wine!"

sentences.zh: 」因泫然流涕，左右莫不歔欷，因宿於佛精舍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears streamed; those at his side none did not sniffle; therefore he lodged overnight in a Buddhist monks' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He wept openly; his men wept with him, and he slept that night in a monastery cell.

sentences.zh: 宣使楊柸、牟皮、牟成、趙生等緣獼猴梯而入，殺韜，置其刀箭而去。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Yang Pei, Mou Pi, Mou Cheng, Zhao Sheng, and others to climb a macaque ladder and enter, killed Tao, placed his knives and arrows, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan sent Yang Pei, Mou Pi, Mou Cheng, and Zhao Sheng up a rope ladder into the hall, murdered Shi Tao, planted the weapons, and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 旦，宣奏之。

translations.literal: At dawn Xuan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Shi Xuan presented the news to court.

sentences.zh: 季龍哀驚氣絕，久之方蘇。

translations.literal: Jilong in grief and shock lost his breath; only after a long time did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu fainted from grief and shock and lay senseless a long while before he stirred.

sentences.zh: 將出臨之，其司空李農諫曰：「害秦公者恐在蕭牆之內，慮生非常，不可以出。

translations.literal: As he was about to go out to attend the body, his minister of works Li Nong remonstrated, saying: "The one who harmed the duke of Qin is probably within the inner walls; I fear something extraordinary will arise; you may not go out."
translations.idiomatic: When he tried to go to the corpse, Li Nong warned, "The hand that killed Prince Qin is likely inside your own household—do not walk into a coup."

sentences.zh: 」季龍乃止。

translations.literal: " Jilong thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu stayed put.

sentences.zh: 嚴兵發哀于太武殿。

translations.literal: With strict troops he held mourning at the Grand Martial Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning under heavy guard in the Grand Martial hall.

sentences.zh: 宣乘素車，從千人，臨韜喪，不哭，直言呵呵，使舉衾看屍，大笑而去。

translations.literal: Xuan rode a plain carriage with a thousand followers, attended Tao's funeral, did not weep, spoke only he-he laughter, had them lift the coverlet to view the corpse, laughed greatly, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan arrived in a plain cart with a thousand men, refused to weep, barked a laugh, had the shroud lifted to leer at the body, and rode off roaring.

sentences.zh: 收大將軍記室參軍鄭靖、尹武等，將委之以罪。

translations.literal: He arrested the grand general's registrar-adjutants Zheng Jing, Yin Wu, and others, intending to pin the crime on them.
translations.idiomatic: He seized registrar-adjutants Zheng Jing and Yin Wu to frame them for the murder.

sentences.zh: 季龍疑宣之害韜也，謀召之，懼其不入，乃偽言其母哀過危惙。

translations.literal: Jilong suspected Xuan had harmed Tao; he plotted to summon him, feared he would not enter, and therefore falsely said his mother's grief had passed into mortal danger.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu guessed Shi Xuan was the killer but dared not summon him cold, so he lied that the prince's mother lay at death's door.

sentences.zh: 宣不虞己之見疑也，入朝中宮，因而止之。

translations.literal: Xuan did not expect that he himself was suspected; he entered to attend the central palace and was therefore detained.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan, never imagining he was suspected, walked into the inner palace and was seized.

sentences.zh: 建興人史科告稱：「韜死夜，宿東宮長上楊柸家,柸夜與五人從外來，相與語曰：『大事已定，但願大家老壽，吾等何患不富貴』。

translations.literal: A man of Jianxing, Shi Ke, reported, saying: "On the night Tao died, I lodged at the eastern-palace chief attendant Yang Pei's house; in the night Pei and five men came from outside and together said: 'The great affair is settled; we only wish our lord long life—how could we fail to grow rich and noble.'".
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ke of Jianxing testified: "The night Shi Tao died I was staying at chief guard Yang Pei's house when Pei and five others slipped in muttering, 'The deed is done—long life to our master and riches for us.'".

sentences.zh: 語訖便入。

translations.literal: When the words ended they entered.
translations.idiomatic: With that they went inside.

sentences.zh: 科寢暗中，柸不見也。

translations.literal: Ke was sleeping in the dark; Pei did not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ke lay hidden in the dark; Pei never saw him.

sentences.zh: 科尋出逃匿。

translations.literal: Ke soon fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: Ke fled at once into hiding.

sentences.zh: 俄而柸與二人出求科不得，柸曰：『宿客聞人向語，當殺之斷口舌。

translations.literal: Before long Pei with two men came out seeking Ke but could not get him; Pei said: "If a lodger overheard people speaking, we ought to kill him to cut off loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pei and two henchmen hunted for Ke, snarling, "Any guest who heard us must die to seal our lips."

sentences.zh: 今而得去，作大事矣。

translations.literal: Now that he has gotten away, he will do a great deed."
translations.idiomatic: "If he escapes, he can ruin everything."

sentences.zh: 』科逾牆獲免。

translations.literal: " Ke climbed over the wall and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ke scaled the wall and escaped.

sentences.zh: 」季龍馳使收之，獲楊柸、牟皮、趙生等。

translations.literal: " Jilong urgently sent agents to arrest them and captured Yang Pei, Mou Pi, Zhao Sheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's runners seized Yang Pei, Mou Pi, and Zhao Sheng.

sentences.zh: 柸、皮尋皆亡去，執趙生而詰之，生具首服。

translations.literal: Pei and Pi soon both fled; they seized Zhao Sheng and interrogated him, and Sheng confessed in full.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and Pi vanished, but Zhao Sheng was taken and confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 季龍悲怒彌甚，幽宣于席庫，以鐵環穿其頷而鎖之，作數斗木槽，和羹飯，以豬狗法食之。

translations.literal: Jilong's grief and rage grew still more severe; he imprisoned Xuan in the mat storehouse, pierced his jaw with an iron ring and locked it, made a wooden trough of several dou capacity, mixed gruel and rice, and fed him by the pig-and-dog method.
translations.idiomatic: Half mad with grief and rage, Shi Hu caged Shi Xuan in the mat depot, ringed his jaw with iron, and fed him slop from a trough like a hog.

sentences.zh: 取害韜刀箭舐其血，哀號震動宮殿。

translations.literal: He took the knives and arrows that had harmed Tao and licked their blood; wailing shook the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Shi Xuan to lick the blades that had killed Shi Tao; the prince's shrieks shook the palace.

sentences.zh: 積柴鄴北，樹標於其上，標末置鹿盧，穿之以繩，倚梯柴積，送宣於標所，使韜所親宦者郝稚、劉霸拔其發，抽其舌，牽之登梯，上于柴積。

translations.literal: They piled firewood north of Ye, set a pole on top, at the pole's tip placed a pulley, threaded it with rope, leaned a ladder on the woodpile, conveyed Xuan to the pole's place, and ordered Tao's intimate eunuchs Hao Zhi and Liu Ba to pull out his hair, draw out his tongue, drag him up the ladder onto the firewood pile.
translations.idiomatic: North of Ye they stacked a pyre, rigged a hoist on a stake, and had Tao's eunuchs Hao Zhi and Liu Ba haul Shi Xuan up by the hair and tongue to the summit.

sentences.zh: 郝稚雙繩貫其頷，鹿盧絞上，劉霸斷其手足，斫眼潰腹，如韜之傷。

translations.literal: Hao Zhi threaded double ropes through his jaw; the pulley winched him upward; Liu Ba severed his hands and feet, gouged his eyes and burst his belly, matching Tao's wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhi ran twin ropes through his jaws and winched him skyward; Liu Ba hacked off his limbs, gouged his eyes, and ripped his belly open to mirror Shi Tao's wounds.

sentences.zh: 四面縱火，煙炎際天。

translations.literal: On the four sides they set fire; smoke and flame reached the sky.
translations.idiomatic: They fired the pyre on every side until smoke licked the heavens.

sentences.zh: 季龍從昭儀已下數千登中臺以觀之。

translations.literal: Jilong ascended the Central Terrace with several thousand persons from imperial concubine rank downward to watch it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu climbed the Central Terrace with thousands of concubines to watch him burn.

sentences.zh: 火滅，取灰分置諸門交道中。

translations.literal: When the fire died, they took the ashes and divided them among the crossroads at the various gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the flames died, they scattered the ashes at every city gate.

sentences.zh: 殺其妻子九人。

translations.literal: They killed his wife and children, nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: They executed his wife and eight children—nine lives in all.

sentences.zh: 宣小子年數歲，季龍甚愛之，抱之而泣。

translations.literal: Xuan's young son was several years old; Jilong loved him greatly and embraced him while weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan's little boy, only a few years old, was a favorite; Shi Hu hugged him and wept.

sentences.zh: 兒曰：「非兒罪。

translations.literal: The child said: "It is not this child's crime."
translations.idiomatic: The child cried, "I did nothing wrong."

sentences.zh: 」季龍欲赦之，其大臣不聽，遂於抱中取而戮之，兒猶挽季龍衣而大叫，時人莫不為之流涕，季龍因此發病。

translations.literal: " Jilong wished to pardon him; his great ministers would not listen; thereupon from within the embrace they took him and executed him; the child still clutched Jilong's robe and screamed greatly; people of the time none did not weep for him; Jilong thereupon fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu meant to spare him, but his ministers refused; they tore the boy from his arms and cut him down while he clung screaming to Shi Hu's robe—every onlooker wept, and the emperor collapsed into illness.

sentences.zh: 又誅其四率已下三百人，宦者五十人，皆車裂節解，棄之漳水。

translations.literal: He also executed more than three hundred men from the four commandants downward, fifty eunuchs, all torn apart by carts and dismembered by joints, and cast them into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred guardsmen below the four commandants and fifty eunuchs were torn apart on carts and dumped in the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 洿其東宮，養豬牛。

translations.literal: He defiled the eastern palace and raised pigs and cattle there.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the eastern palace into a sty for pigs and oxen.

sentences.zh: 東宮衛士十餘萬人皆謫戍涼州。

translations.literal: More than one hundred thousand eastern-palace guardsmen were all banished to garrison Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred thousand eastern-palace guards were stripped and sent to the Liangzhou frontier.

sentences.zh: 先是，散騎常侍趙攬言于季龍曰：「中宮將有變，宜防之。

translations.literal: Earlier, attendant cavalier Zhao Lan had said to Jilong: "The central palace will have a change; you ought to guard against it."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhao Lan had warned Shi Hu, "The inner palace will turn violent—take care."

sentences.zh: 」及宣之殺韜也，季龍疑其知而不告，亦誅之。

translations.literal: " When Xuan killed Tao, Jilong suspected that he had known but not reported, and executed him too.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xuan murdered Shi Tao, Shi Hu decided Zhao Lan had known and said nothing, and killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 廢宣母杜氏為庶人。

translations.literal: He demoted Xuan's mother Lady Du to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced Shi Xuan's mother, Lady Du, to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪柳氏，尚書耆之女也，以才色特幸，坐其二兄有寵于宣，亦殺之。

translations.literal: Honored concubine Lady Liu was the daughter of Masters-of-Writing Liu Qi; by talent and beauty she had won special favor; because her two elder brothers had won favor with Xuan, she too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu the honored concubine—daughter of Liu Qi of the secretariat—had dazzled the harem, but because her brothers had curried Shi Xuan's favor she was put to death too.

sentences.zh: 季龍追其姿色，復納耆少女于華林園。

translations.literal: Jilong pursued her beauty and again took into the Hualin Garden a young girl of Qi's family.
translations.idiomatic: Still lusting after that beauty, Shi Hu installed another young daughter of the Liu clan in Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 季龍議立太子，其太尉張舉進曰：「燕公斌、彭城公遵並有武藝文德。

translations.literal: When Jilong deliberated on establishing an heir apparent, his grand commandant Zhang Ju advanced and said: "The duke of Yan, Bin, and the duke of Pengcheng, Zun, together possess martial skill and civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Discussing the succession, grand commandant Zhang Ju said, "Prince Yan Shi Bin and Prince Pengcheng Shi Zun both combine civil talent with military prowess."

sentences.zh: 陛下神齒已衰，四海未一，請擇二公而樹之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's divine years are already declining; within the four seas there is not yet unity; please choose between the two dukes and establish one."
translations.idiomatic: "Your strength is failing and the realm still divided—choose between these two princes and name an heir."

sentences.zh: 」初，戎昭張豺之破上邽也，獲劉曜幼女，年十二，有殊色，季龍得而嬖之，生子世，封齊公。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when the martial-brilliance general Zhang Chai had broken Shanggui, he had captured Liu Yao's youngest daughter; she was twelve years old and of extraordinary beauty; Jilong obtained her and doted on her; she bore a son, Shi Shi, who was enfeoffed duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when Zhang Chai took Shanggui, he had captured Liu Yao's twelve-year-old daughter of rare beauty; Shi Hu made her his consort, and she bore their son Shi Shi, later enfeoffed duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 至是，豺以季龍年長多疾，規立世為嗣，劉當為太后，己得輔政，說季龍曰：「陛下再立儲宮，皆出自倡賤，是以禍亂相尋。

translations.literal: At this point Chai, because Jilong was advanced in years and often ill, plotted to establish Shi as heir so that Liu would become empress dowager and he himself could assist rule; he urged Jilong, saying: "Your Majesty has twice established a heir's palace; both came from singing-girls of low status; therefore disasters have followed one after the other.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang Chai, seeing Shi Hu old and ailing, schemed to put Shi Shi on the throne so Lady Liu could rule as dowager and he could govern; he argued, "Every heir you have named rose from lowborn entertainers—that is why turmoil never ends."

sentences.zh: 今宜擇母貴子孝者立之。

translations.literal: Now you ought to choose one whose mother is noble and whose son is filial and establish him."
translations.idiomatic: "Pick a son with a highborn mother and a filial heart."

sentences.zh: 」季龍曰：「卿且勿言，吾知太子處矣。

translations.literal: " Jilong said: "Minister, for the moment do not speak; We know where the heir shall be."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu cut him short: "Say no more—I already know where the crown will rest."

sentences.zh: 」又議於東堂，季龍曰：「吾欲以純灰三斛洗吾腹，腹穢惡，故生凶子，兒年二十餘便欲殺公。

translations.literal: " Again they deliberated in the Eastern Hall; Jilong said: "We wish to wash Our belly with three hu of pure ash; Our belly is foul and evil, therefore it bore vicious sons; at twenty-some years they already wished to kill a lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Hall he raged, "I would scour my belly with three hu of quicklime—my own bowels bred beasts who at twenty wanted their father's blood."

sentences.zh: 今世方十歲，比其二十，吾已老矣。

translations.literal: Now Shi is only ten years old; by the time he reaches twenty, We shall already be old."
translations.idiomatic: "Shi Shi is only ten; when he turns twenty I shall be a spent man."

sentences.zh: 」於是與張舉、李農定議，敕公卿上書請立世。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with Zhang Ju and Li Nong he fixed the decision and ordered the dukes and ministers to submit memorials requesting that Shi Shi be established.
translations.idiomatic: He then settled the matter with Zhang Ju and Li Nong and ordered the high ministers to memorialize for Shi Shi's enthronement as heir.

sentences.zh: 大司農曹莫不署名，季龍使張豺問其故。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Cao Mo did not affix his signature; Jilong sent Zhang Chai to ask him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Minister of Agriculture Cao Mo withheld his signature, Shi Hu sent Zhang Chai to demand an explanation.

sentences.zh: 莫頓首曰：「天下業重，不宜立少，是以不敢署也。

translations.literal: Mo knocked his head on the ground and said: "The enterprise of All-under-Heaven is weighty; it is not fitting to establish the young; therefore I dare not sign."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mo kowtowed and said, "The realm is too grave a burden for a child—that is why I could not set my name to it."

sentences.zh: 」季龍曰：「莫，忠臣也，然未達朕意。

translations.literal: " Jilong said: "Mo is a loyal subject, yet he has not grasped Our intention."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu replied, "Cao Mo is a faithful minister; he simply does not see what I mean."

sentences.zh: 張舉、李農知吾心矣，其令諭之。

translations.literal: Zhang Ju and Li Nong know Our mind; order them to explain it to him."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang Ju and Li Nong already understand my purpose—have them make it clear to him."

sentences.zh: 」遂立世為皇太子，劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he established Shi as heir apparent and the Liu clan woman as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He then named Shi Shi crown prince and invested Lady Liu as empress.

sentences.zh: 季龍召太常條攸、光祿勳杜嘏謂之曰：「煩卿傅太子，實希改轍，吾之相托，卿宜明之。

translations.literal: Jilong summoned Grand Master of Ceremonies Tiao You and Superintendent of the Household Du Gu and said to them: "We trouble you two to tutor the heir; We truly hope for a change of course; as for Our entrusting this matter to you, you ought to understand it clearly."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu called in Tiao You, grand master of ceremonies, and Du Gu, superintendent of the household, and told them, "I ask you to school the heir and truly wish him to mend his ways; what I am handing you, you must take to heart."

sentences.zh: 」署攸太傅，嘏為少傅。

translations.literal: " He appointed You grand tutor and Gu junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He named Tiao You grand tutor and Du Gu junior tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 季龍時疾瘳，以僭即皇帝位於南郊，大赦境內，建元曰太寧。

translations.literal: When at that time Jilong's illness had abated, he usurped the imperial title at the southern suburb, granted a general amnesty within the borders, and established the era name Great Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Hu had rallied from his sickness, he arrogated the throne at the southern suburban altar, proclaimed an empire-wide amnesty, and adopted the reign title Tauning.

sentences.zh: 百官增位一等，諸子進爵郡王。

translations.literal: All officials had their positions raised one grade; his various sons were advanced in noble rank to princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister gained a step in rank, and his sons were promoted to princes of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 以尚書張良為右僕射。

translations.literal: He appointed Masters-of-Writing Zhang Liang as right vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang of the secretariat was made right vice-director.

sentences.zh: 故東宮謫卒高力等萬餘人當戍涼州，行達雍城，既不在赦例，又敕雍州刺史張茂送之。

translations.literal: Former eastern-palace degraded soldiers called the Gao Li, more than ten thousand men, were due to be garrisoned in Liangzhou; en route they reached Yongcheng; they were not within the categories of amnesty, and moreover an edict ordered Yongzhou Governor Zhang Mao to escort them on.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand demoted eastern-palace toughs known as the Gao Li were bound for Liangzhou; when they reached Yongcheng they fell outside the amnesty, and the throne ordered Governor Zhang Mao to march them onward.

sentences.zh: 茂皆奪其馬，令步推鹿車，致糧戍所。

translations.literal: Mao seized all their horses, ordered them to go on foot pushing deer carts, and had grain delivered to the garrison place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao confiscated their mounts and made them haul supplies on foot in handcarts all the way to the posting.

sentences.zh: 高力督定陽梁犢等害眾心之怨，謀起兵東還，陰令胡人頡獨鹿微告戍者，戍者皆踴抃大呼。

translations.literal: Gao Li supervisor Liang Du of Dingyang and others nursed the resentment boiling in every breast, plotted to raise troops and return east, secretly ordered the Hu man Xiedulu to hint to the garrison men, and the garrison men all leaped, clapped, and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: Their overseer Liang Du of Dingyang and his comrades, burning with the men's grievances, plotted an eastern mutiny; Xiedulu quietly tipped off the conscripts, who burst into cheers and stamped their approval.

sentences.zh: 梁犢乃自稱晉征東大將軍，率眾攻陷下辯，逼張茂為大都督、大司馬，載以軺車。

translations.literal: Liang Du then styled himself Jin's General Who Conquers the East, led the host to storm and take Xiabian, compelled Zhang Mao to become grand commander-in-chief and grand marshal, and conveyed him in a light carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Du declared himself Jin's eastern-expedition commander, seized Xiabian, forced Zhang Mao to take the titles of grand commander and grand marshal, and paraded him in an open coach.

sentences.zh: 安西劉甯自安定擊之，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Anxi Liu Ning struck them from Anding and was greatly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning, the western pacifier, attacked from Anding and limped back in rout.

sentences.zh: 秦、雍間城戍無不摧陷，斬二千石長史，長驅而東。

translations.literal: Between Qin and Yong no city garrison failed to be shattered; they beheaded administrators of two-thousand-shi salary rank and drove straight east.
translations.idiomatic: Fort after fort between Qin and Yong fell; they slew salary-rank governors and swept eastward without pause.

sentences.zh: 高力等皆多力善射，一當十餘人，雖無兵甲，所在掠百姓大斧，施一丈柯，攻戰若神，所向崩潰，戍卒皆隨之，比至長安，眾已十萬。

translations.literal: The Gao Li and their like were all strong of arm and skilled at archery; one man matched more than ten; though they lacked armor and weapons, wherever they went they plundered the common people's great axes, fitted shafts of one zhang, fought as if divine, and wherever they aimed lines collapsed; garrison troops all followed them; by the time they reached Chang'an, the host already numbered one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Those Gao Li fighters were archers and brawlers who could each hold off a dozen men; unarmed, they seized farmers' broadaxes, mounted them on ten-foot helves, and swept through defenses like spirits until every garrison joined them—by Chang'an their horde had swollen to a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 其樂平王石苞時鎮長安，盡銳距之，一戰而敗。

translations.literal: Prince of Leping Shi Bao at that time was stationed at Chang'an; he committed his sharpest troops to resisting them and was defeated in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao, prince of Leping, held Chang'an and threw his best troops against the rebels, only to lose at the first clash.

sentences.zh: 犢遂東出潼關，進如洛川。

translations.literal: Liang Du then went east out of Tong Pass and advanced toward the Luochuan region.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Du broke east through Tong Pass and rolled on toward the Luoyang basin.

sentences.zh: 季龍以李農為大都督，行大將軍事，統衛軍張賀度、征西張良、征虜石閔等，率步騎十萬討之。

translations.literal: Jilong appointed Li Nong as grand commander-in-chief, acting grand general's duties, commanding guards-army Zhang Hedu, western campaign Zhang Liang, captive-quelling Shi Min, and others, and led one hundred thousand infantry and horse to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu named Li Nong commander-in-chief with plenipotentiary general's powers, put Zhang Hedu, Zhang Liang, Shi Min, and others under him, and sent a hundred thousand horse and foot to crush the rising.

sentences.zh: 戰于新安，農師不利。

translations.literal: They fought at Xin'an; Li Nong's army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Battle joined at Xin'an, and Li Nong's line buckled.

sentences.zh: 又戰于洛陽，農師又敗，乃退壁成皋。

translations.literal: Again they fought at Luoyang; Li Nong's army was again defeated; thereupon he withdrew and fortified at Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: A second clash at Luoyang broke him again, so he pulled back and dug in at Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 犢東掠滎陽、陳留諸郡，季龍大懼，以燕王石斌為大都督中外諸軍事，率精騎一萬，統姚弋仲、苻洪等擊犢于滎陽東，大敗之，斬犢首而還，討其餘黨，盡滅之。

translations.literal: Liang Du raided east through Xingyang, Chenliu, and the various commanderies; Jilong was greatly afraid; he appointed Prince of Yan Shi Bin as grand commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without, led ten thousand picked cavalry, commanded Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, and others, and struck Liang Du east of Xingyang, greatly defeated him, beheaded Liang Du and returned, punished his remaining faction, and utterly extinguished them.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang Du pillaged Xingyang and Chenliu, Shi Hu panicked; he gave Shi Bin, prince of Yan, supreme command, ten thousand elite riders, and lieutenants Yao Yizhong and Fu Hong, shattered Liang Du east of Xingyang, brought back his head, and extirpated the rest of his party.

sentences.zh: 俄而晉將軍王龕拔其沛郡。

translations.literal: Before long Jin general Wang Kan captured their Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin's Wang Kan ripped Pei commandery from Zhao hands.

sentences.zh: 始平人馬勖起兵于洛氏葛谷，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: A man of Shiping, Ma Xu, raised troops at Luoshi Ge Valley and styled himself general.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xu of Shiping rose in Luoshi Ge Valley and proclaimed himself a general.

sentences.zh: 石苞攻滅之，誅三千餘家。

translations.literal: Shi Bao attacked and destroyed him, executing more than three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao stamped out the band and put over three thousand households to the sword.

sentences.zh: 時熒惑犯積屍，又犯昴、月，及熒惑北犯河鼓。

translations.literal: At that time Mars encroached on the Pile of Corpses asterism, also encroached on Mao and the moon, and Mars went north to encroach on River Drum.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent Mars across the Pile of Corpses, across the Pleiades and the moon, and north toward the River Drum stars—a grim sky.

sentences.zh: 未幾，季龍疾甚，以石遵為大將軍，鎮關右，石斌為丞相、錄尚書事，張豺為鎮衛大將軍、領軍將軍、吏部尚書，並受遺輔政。

translations.literal: Before long Jilong's illness was severe; he appointed Shi Zun as grand general guarding the land west of the passes, Shi Bin as chancellor and recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, Zhang Chai as grand general who guards the realm, commanding-general of the army, and minister of personnel, all receiving testamentary mandate to assist rule.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu soon sank mortally ill; he named Shi Zun grand general for the Guanzhong west, Shi Bin chancellor with custody of the secretariat, and Zhang Chai capital guardian, army commander, and personnel minister—each charged by deathbed edict to steer the state.

sentences.zh: 劉氏懼斌之輔政也害世，與張豺謀誅之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu feared that if Bin assisted rule he would harm Shi; she plotted with Zhang Chai to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu feared Shi Bin as regent would murder young Shi Shi; she conspired with Zhang Chai to kill him first.

sentences.zh: 斌時在襄國，乃遣使詐斌曰：「主上患已漸損，王須獵者，可小停也。

translations.literal: Bin was at Xiangguo; she then sent an envoy falsely telling Bin: "The sovereign's ailment has gradually lessened; if the king needs hunting, he may pause a little."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin was in Xiangguo; she sent a messenger with a lie: "The emperor is mending; if you mean to hunt, you may linger awhile."

sentences.zh: 」斌性好酒耽獵，遂遊畋縱飲。

translations.literal: Bin by nature loved wine and was addicted to hunting; thereupon he roamed hunting and drank without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin loved wine and the chase; he gave himself to hunts and drinking binges.

sentences.zh: 劉氏矯命稱斌無忠孝之心，免斌官，以王歸第，使張豺弟雄率龍騰五百人守之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu forged orders saying Bin lacked loyal and filial heart, dismissed Bin from office, ordered him as a prince to return to his mansion, and sent Zhang Chai's brother Zhang Xiong leading five hundred Dragon Surge troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: She forged an edict accusing Shi Bin of disloyalty, stripped his offices, sent the prince home under house arrest, and posted Zhang Xiong with five hundred Dragon Surge guards.

sentences.zh: 石遵自幽州至鄴，敕朝堂受拜，配禁兵三萬遣之，遵慟泣而去。

translations.literal: Shi Zun came from Youzhou to Ye; he was ordered to receive appointment at the court hall, was allotted thirty thousand palace guards and dispatched; Zun wept bitterly and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun rode from Youzhou to Ye, was made to take his commission in open court, handed thirty thousand household troops, and sent away weeping.

sentences.zh: 是日季龍疾小瘳，問曰：「遵至未？

translations.literal: That day Jilong's illness slightly abated; he asked: "Has Zun arrived?"
translations.idiomatic: That same day Shi Hu briefly rallied and asked, "Has Shi Zun come?"

sentences.zh: 」左右答言久已去矣。

translations.literal: " Those at his side answered that long ago he had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said he had left long since.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「恨不見之。

translations.literal: Jilong said: "We regret not having seen him."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu murmured, "How I wish I could have seen him."

sentences.zh: 」季龍臨於西閣，龍騰將軍、中郎二百餘人列拜於前。

translations.literal: " Jilong attended at the western gallery; more than two hundred Dragon Surge generals and gentlemen-of-the-household lined up and bowed before him.
translations.idiomatic: He received them at the western gallery, where over two hundred Dragon Surge officers and household gentlemen bowed in ranks.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「何所求也？

translations.literal: Jilong said: "What do you seek?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked what they wanted of him.

sentences.zh: 」皆言聖躬不和，宜令燕王入宿衛，典兵馬，或言乞為皇太子。

translations.literal: " They all said the sacred person was unwell; Yan Wang ought to enter to guard overnight and command troops and horses; some begged to become crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded that the sovereign was failing and the prince of Yan should enter to command the guard; others clamored to be named heir.

sentences.zh: 季龍不知斌之廢也，責曰：「燕王不在內邪？

translations.literal: Jilong did not know Bin had been dismissed; he rebuked them, saying: "Is not the Prince of Yan within?"
translations.idiomatic: Unaware Shi Bin had been cashiered, Shi Hu snapped, "Is not the prince of Yan already inside?"

sentences.zh: 呼來！

translations.literal: Call him here!"
translations.idiomatic: "Summon him at once!"

sentences.zh: 」左右言王酒病，不能入。

translations.literal: " Those at his side said the king was ill from wine and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: They answered that the prince was drunk-sick and could not come.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「促持輦迎之，當付其璽綬。

translations.literal: Jilong said: "Hurry—take a palanquin to welcome him; We shall hand him the seals and cords."
translations.idiomatic: "Send a litter—quickly," Shi Hu ordered. "I will give him the seals myself."

sentences.zh: 」亦竟無行者。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end none went.
translations.idiomatic: No one moved to obey.

sentences.zh: 尋昏眩而入。

translations.literal: Shortly he entered in dizziness.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he collapsed into a stupor.

sentences.zh: 張豺使弟雄等矯季龍命殺斌，劉氏又矯命以豺為太保、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，加千兵百騎，一依霍光輔漢故事。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai had his brother Xiong and others forge Jilong's order to kill Bin; Lady Liu again forged orders appointing Zhang Chai grand guardian, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, adding a thousand infantry and hundred horse in guard, entirely according to the precedent of Huo Guang assisting Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai's brother Xiong forged an order executing Shi Bin; Liu forged another elevating Zhang Chai to grand guardian, supreme commander, and secretariat overseer with a thousand foot and a hundred horse—aping Huo Guang's regency over Han.

sentences.zh: 侍中徐統歎曰：「禍將作矣，吾無為豫之。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-chief Xu Tong sighed: "Calamity is about to arise; I will not put myself among those who prepare for it beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Xu Tong groaned, "The storm is coming—I want no part of the schemes ahead."

sentences.zh: 」乃仰藥而死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed poison and died.

sentences.zh: 俄而季龍亦死。

translations.literal: Before long Jilong also died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Hu followed him to the grave.

sentences.zh: 季龍始以僭立，至此，凡在位十五歲。

translations.literal: Jilong had begun by usurping the throne; reaching this point, altogether he had occupied the throne fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: From his seizure of the throne to this hour Shi Hu had reigned fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 石世

translations.literal: Shi Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Heading: Shi Shi.

sentences.zh: 於是世即偽位，尊劉氏為皇太后，臨朝，進張豺為丞相。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi succeeded to the false throne, honored Lady Liu as empress dowager with court regency, and advanced Zhang Chai to chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi mounted the puppet throne, raised Lady Liu to ruling empress dowager, and made Zhang Chai chancellor.

sentences.zh: 豺請石遵、石鑒為左右丞相，以尉其心，劉氏從之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai requested Shi Zun and Shi Jian as left and right chancellors to soothe their hearts; Lady Liu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai named Shi Zun and Shi Jian left and right chancellors to buy their loyalty; Liu agreed.

sentences.zh: 豺與張舉謀誅李農，而舉與農素善，以豺謀告之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai plotted with Zhang Ju to kill Li Nong, but Zhang Ju was on good terms with Li Nong and informed Li Nong of Zhang Chai's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai and Zhang Ju planned Li Nong's murder, yet Zhang Ju, Li Nong's friend, leaked the plot.

sentences.zh: 農懼，率騎百餘奔廣宗，率乞活數萬家保于上白。

translations.literal: Li Nong feared, led more than a hundred horsemen and fled to Guangzong, and led several tens of thousands of Qiehuo households to hold Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Li Nong galloped to Guangzong with a hundred riders and rallied tens of thousands of Qiehuo refugee families on Mount Shangbai.

sentences.zh: 劉氏使張舉等統宿衛精卒圍之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu sent Zhang Ju and others to command elite palace-guard troops to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu dispatched Zhang Ju with the household elite to invest the mountain.

sentences.zh: 豺以張離為鎮軍大將軍、監中外諸軍事、司隸校尉，為己之副。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai appointed Zhang Li as grand general who stabilizes the army, overseer of all military affairs within and without, metropolitan governor, as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai made Zhang Li army-stabilizing commander, overseer of all forces, metropolitan governor, and his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 鄴中群盜大起，迭相劫掠。

translations.literal: In Ye bandits arose in great numbers, repeatedly raiding one another.
translations.idiomatic: Ye erupted in robbery as gangs preyed on one another.

sentences.zh: 石遵聞季龍之死，屯於河內。

translations.literal: When Shi Zun heard of Jilong's death, he encamped at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Shi Hu's death, Shi Zun halted his army at Henei.

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲、苻洪、石閔、劉甯及武衛王鸞、甯西王午、石榮、王鐵、立義將軍段勤等既平秦、洛，班師而歸，遇遵于李城，說遵曰：「殿下長而且賢，先帝亦有意于殿下矣。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, Shi Min, Liu Ning, and martial guard Wang Luan, western pacification Wang Wu, Shi Rong, Wang Tie, righteous-establishment general Duan Qin and others, having pacified Qin and Luo, rotated the army home, met Zun at Licheng, and urged Zun, saying: "Your Highness is eldest and worthy; the late emperor also had intentions toward Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, Shi Min, Liu Ning, Wang Luan of the martial guard, Wang Wu of western pacification, Shi Rong, Wang Tie, Duan Qin the righteous-establishment general, and the rest—fresh from pacifying Qin and Luoyang—ran into Shi Zun at Licheng and pleaded, "You are the eldest worthy prince, and the late emperor already favored you."

sentences.zh: 但以末年惛惑，為張豺所誤。

translations.literal: Only because in his closing years he was muddled and deluded was he misled by Zhang Chai.
translations.idiomatic: Only his final confusion let Zhang Chai lead him astray.

sentences.zh: 今上白相持未下，京師宿衛空虛，若聲張豺之罪，鼓行而討之，孰不倒戈開門而迎殿下者邪！

translations.literal: Now Shangbai still stalemates unconquered; the capital's palace guard stands empty; if we proclaim Zhang Chai's crimes and march with drums beating to punish him, who would not turn halberds and open gates to welcome Your Highness!
translations.idiomatic: Shangbai still holds out and the capital guard is hollow—denounce Zhang Chai and march in formation, and every soldier will drop his weapon and throw open the gates for you!

sentences.zh: 」遵從之。

translations.literal: Zun followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun took their counsel.

sentences.zh: 洛州刺史劉國等亦率洛陽之眾至於李城。

translations.literal: Luozhou Governor Liu Guo and others also led Luoyang's host and arrived at Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guo, governor of Luozhou, marched the Luoyang garrison to join them at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 遵檄至鄴，張豺大懼，馳召上白之軍。

translations.literal: When Zun's proclamation reached Ye, Zhang Chai was greatly afraid and urgently recalled the army at Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai panicked when Shi Zun's manifesto hit Ye and frantically pulled the Shangbai siege army home.

sentences.zh: 遵次於蕩陰，戎卒九萬，石閔為前鋒。

translations.literal: Zun halted at Dangyin; field troops numbered ninety thousand; Shi Min was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun camped at Dangyin with ninety thousand veterans and Shi Min spearheading the column.

sentences.zh: 豺將出距之，耆舊羯士皆曰：「天子兒來奔喪，吾當出迎之，不能為張豺城戍也。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chai was about to go out to resist them, the elderly Jie warriors all said: "The Son of Heaven's son has come to mourn the funeral; we ought to go out to welcome him; we cannot be wall-and-garrison men for Zhang Chai."
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Chai prepared to meet them in the field, gray-haired Jie soldiers shouted, "The emperor's son rides to bury his father—we should welcome him, not man Zhang Chai's ramparts."

sentences.zh: 」逾城而出，豺斬之不能止。

translations.literal: They climbed over the walls and went out; Zhang Chai executed them but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: They scaled the walls to desert; Zhang Chai slaughtered them but could not stem the tide.

sentences.zh: 張離率龍騰二千斬關迎遵。

translations.literal: Zhang Li led two thousand Dragon Surge troops to cut through the barrier and welcome Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li smashed a gate with two thousand Dragon Surge troops and ushered Shi Zun inside.

sentences.zh: 劉氏懼，引張豺入，對之悲哭曰：「先帝梓宮未殯，而禍難繁興。

translations.literal: Lady Liu feared, led Zhang Chai in, and wept miserably to him, saying: "The late emperor's catafalque has not yet been buried, yet disasters multiply and arise."
translations.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, Lady Liu drew Zhang Chai in and sobbed, "The late ruler still lies unburied while calamities pile up."

sentences.zh: 今皇嗣沖幼，托之于將軍，將軍何以匡濟邪？

translations.literal: Now the imperial heir is young and tender; We entrust him to you, general—how will you rescue and aid?
translations.idiomatic: The boy on the throne is helpless—I lean on you, general—how will you save us?

sentences.zh: 加遵重官，可以弭不？

translations.literal: Add Zun high office—can it quell this?
translations.idiomatic: Would stacking honors on Shi Zun quiet this storm?

sentences.zh: 」豺惶怖失守，無復籌計，但言唯唯。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai was panic-stricken and lost his guard, had no further schemes, and only said yes-yes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai went blank with fright, offered no plan, and muttered empty assent.

sentences.zh: 劉氏令以遵為丞相、領大司馬、大都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，加黃鉞、九錫，增封十郡，委以阿衡之任。

translations.literal: Lady Liu ordered Zun appointed chancellor, concurrently grand marshal, grand commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, adding golden battle-axe and nine bestowals, increasing fief by ten commanderies, entrusting him with the burden of prime minister like Yi Yin.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered Shi Zun made chancellor, grand marshal, supreme commander, secretariat overseer, golden-axe bearer, nine-insignia recipient, and holder of ten added commanderies—the full weight of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 遵至安陽亭，張豺懼而出迎，遵命執之。

translations.literal: When Zun reached Anyang pavilion, Zhang Chai feared and came out to welcome him; Zun ordered him seized.
translations.idiomatic: At Anyang pavilion Zhang Chai crept out to greet Shi Zun, who had him arrested on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是貫甲曜兵，入自鳳陽門，升于太武前殿，擗踴盡哀，退如東閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon they donned armor and displayed weapons, entered by Fengyang Gate, ascended the Grand Martial front hall, beat their breasts and stamped in full mourning, then withdrew to the eastern gallery.
translations.idiomatic: Armored and banners blazing, they entered through Fengyang Gate, climbed the Grand Martial hall to keen and drum their grief, then retired to the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 斬張豺于平樂市，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai was beheaded at Pingle market; his three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai died on the Pingle market scaffold, his three kinships extirpated.

sentences.zh: 假劉氏令曰：「嗣子幼沖，先帝私恩所授，皇業至重，非所克堪。

translations.literal: Forging Lady Liu's order it said: "The heir is young and tender; he was appointed by the late emperor's private favor; the imperial enterprise is supremely weighty—not what he can bear."
translations.idiomatic: A forged rescript in Liu's voice read, "The boy was enthroned by a father's whim; the mandate is too vast for him."

sentences.zh: 其以遵嗣位。

translations.literal: Let Zun succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Let Shi Zun inherit the throne.

sentences.zh: 」遵偽讓至於再三，群臣敦勸，乃受之，僭即尊位於太武前殿，大赦殊死已下，罷上白圍。

translations.literal: Zun falsely declined reaching thrice; the ministers urgently urged; then he accepted, usurped the supreme title at the Grand Martial front hall, granted general amnesty short of capital crimes, and lifted the siege of Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun thrice refused the crown until his ministers pressed him; then he seized the throne in the Grand Martial hall, granted a general amnesty short of capital crimes, and raised the siege of Shangbai.

sentences.zh: 封世為譙王，邑萬戶待以不臣之禮，廢劉氏為太妃，尋皆殺之。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Shi as Prince of Qiao with ten thousand households and treated him with the rites due one who is not a subject; he demoted Lady Liu to senior consort; before long both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He made Shi Shi prince of Qiao with a ten-thousand-household fief yet honored him like a peer, reduced Lady Liu to senior consort, and soon murdered them both.

sentences.zh: 世凡立三十三日。

translations.literal: Shi had altogether occupied the position thirty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi had ruled thirty-three days in all.

sentences.zh: 石遵

translations.literal: Shi Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Heading: Shi Zun.

sentences.zh: 於是李農歸請罪，遵復其位，待之如初。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Nong returned to ask forgiveness; Zun restored his position and treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong came back to plead guilt; Shi Zun restored his offices and favored him as before.

sentences.zh: 尊其母鄭氏為皇太后，其妻張氏為皇后，以石斌子衍為皇太子，石鑒為侍中，石沖為太保，石苞為大司馬，石琨為大將軍，石閔為中外諸軍事、輔國大將軍、錄尚書事，輔政。

translations.literal: He honored his mother Lady Zheng as empress dowager, his wife Lady Zhang as empress, appointed Shi Bin's son Yan as crown prince, Shi Jian as attendant-in-chief, Shi Chong as grand guardian, Shi Bao as grand marshal, Shi Kun as grand general, Shi Min as overseer of all military affairs within and without, grand general who aids the state, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, assisting rule.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Lady Zheng to empress dowager, Lady Zhang to empress, named Shi Yan—Shi Bin's son—heir apparent, Shi Jian palace attendant, Shi Chong grand guardian, Shi Bao grand marshal, Shi Kun commander-in-chief, and Shi Min supreme military overseer, state-aiding grand general, and secretariat regent.

sentences.zh: 暴風拔樹，震雷，雨雹大如盂升。

translations.literal: A violent wind uprooted trees; shaking thunder; hail fell as large as bowls and sheng-measures.
translations.idiomatic: Gales tore up timber, thunder cracked, and hailstones wide as bowls hammered the capital.

sentences.zh: 太武、暉華殿災，諸門觀閣蕩然，其乘輿服御燒者太半，光焰照天，金石皆盡，火月餘乃滅。

translations.literal: Grand Martial and Huihua halls suffered fire disaster; gates, towers, and galleries were swept bare; of imperial carriages and wardrobe those burned were more than half; light and flame illumined heaven; metal and stone were all consumed; the fire after more than a month then died.
translations.idiomatic: Flames gutted the Grand Martial and Huihua halls, stripped gates and belvederes bare, and consumed more than half the chariots and robes—molten metal glared skyward for over a month before the blaze died.

sentences.zh: 雨血周遍鄴城。

translations.literal: Blood rain fell everywhere throughout Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Rain the color of blood drenched every ward of Ye.

sentences.zh: 石沖時鎮于薊，聞遵殺世而自立，乃謂其僚佐曰：「世受先帝之命，遵輒廢殺，罪逆莫大，其敕內外戎嚴，孤將親討之。

translations.literal: Shi Chong at that time was stationed at Ji; hearing Zun had killed Shi and established himself, he said to his staff and aides: "Shi received the late emperor's mandate; Zun abruptly deposed and killed him—the crime of rebellion is greatest; order inner and outer to tighten armor; I myself will personally punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong held Ji when news came that Shi Zun had murdered Shi Shi and seized power; he told his advisers, "The boy bore the late emperor's charge—Shi Zun slew him by treason; seal the passes—I march myself to punish him."

sentences.zh: 」於是留寧北沭堅戍幽州，帥眾五萬，自薊討遵，傳檄燕、趙，所在雲集，比及常山，眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he left northern pacification Mu Jian to garrison Youzhou, led a host of fifty thousand, from Ji punished Zun, transmitted proclamations through Yan and Zhao; wherever they went clouds gathered; by the time they reached Changshan, the host exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He left Mu Jian of northern pacification to hold Youzhou, took fifty thousand men from Ji, broadcast manifestos across Yan and Zhao until recruits swarmed in—beyond Changshan his army topped a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 次於苑鄉，遇遵赦書，謂左右曰：「吾弟一也，死者不可復追，何為復相殘乎！

translations.literal: He halted at Yuanxiang; encountering Zun's amnesty edict, he said to those at his side: "My younger brother and I are one; the dead cannot be pursued back—why again mutually injure one another!"
translations.idiomatic: Camped at Yuanxiang, he read Shi Zun's pardon and mused aloud, "He is still my brother—the dead cannot return; why should we cut one another down again!"

sentences.zh: 吾將歸矣。

translations.literal: I shall return.
translations.idiomatic: I am going home.

sentences.zh: 」其將陳暹進曰：「彭城篡弑自尊，為罪大矣。

translations.literal: His general Chen Xian advanced saying: "The prince of Pengcheng usurped and murdered to honor himself—the crime is great."
translations.idiomatic: General Chen Xian cut in, "The prince of Pengcheng murdered his way to the throne—the guilt is monstrous."

sentences.zh: 王雖北旆，臣將南轅，平京師，擒彭城，然後奉迎大駕。

translations.literal: Though Your Highness turns the banner north, your servant will turn the axle south, pacify the capital, capture the prince of Pengcheng, then welcome the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: You may wheel north, my lord, but I will drive south, seize the capital, cage the prince of Pengcheng, and only then escort your majesty home.

sentences.zh: 」沖從之。

translations.literal: Chong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong agreed.

sentences.zh: 遵馳遣王擢以書喻沖，沖弗聽。

translations.literal: Zun urgently sent Wang Zhuo with a letter to enlighten Chong; Chong did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun raced Wang Zhuo ahead with a letter dissuading Shi Chong, who ignored it.

sentences.zh: 遵假石閔黃鉞、金鉦，與李農等率精卒十萬討之。

translations.literal: Zun lent Shi Min the yellow battle-axe and golden cymbals; together with Li Nong and others he led one hundred thousand elite troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun handed Shi Min the yellow axe and golden bells; with Li Nong and others he marched one hundred thousand picked troops against the rebel.

sentences.zh: 戰于平棘，沖師大敗，獲沖於元氏，賜死，坑其士卒三萬餘人。

translations.literal: They fought at Pingji; Chong's army was greatly defeated; Chong was captured at Yuanshi, granted death, and more than thirty thousand of his soldiers were buried alive in pits.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingji Shi Chong's host shattered; taken at Yuanshi he was forced to kill himself, and thirty thousand of his men were buried alive in mass graves.

sentences.zh: 始葬季龍，號其墓為顯原陵，偽諡武皇帝，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: They began burying Jilong; his tomb was titled Manifest Plain Mound; false posthumous title Martial Emperor; temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: They laid Shi Hu to rest on Manifest Plain tumulus, posthumously dubbing him Martial Emperor with temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 遵揚州刺史王浹以淮南歸順。

translations.literal: Zun's Yangzhou Governor Wang Jie brought Huainan to allegiance in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun's Yangzhou governor Wang Jie delivered Huainan to Jin in submission.

sentences.zh: 晉西中郎將陳逵進據壽春。

translations.literal: Jin's western gentleman-general Chen Kui advanced and occupied Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's western camp general Chen Kui marched in and seized Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍褚裒率師伐遵，次於下邳，遵以李農為南討大都督，率騎二萬來距。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou led troops to punish Zun and halted at Xiapi; Zun appointed Li Nong grand commander-in-chief of the southern expedition and led twenty thousand horse to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou drove north against Shi Zun and camped at Xiapi; Shi Zun made Li Nong southern-expedition commander-in-chief and sent twenty thousand riders to block him.

sentences.zh: 裒不能進，退屯廣陵。

translations.literal: Pou could not advance and withdrew to encamp at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou could not push forward and fell back to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 陳逵聞之，懼，遂焚壽春積聚，毀城而還。

translations.literal: When Chen Kui heard this, he feared, thereupon burned Shouchun's stored supplies, destroyed the walls, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui panicked at the news, torched the Shouchun granaries, dismantled the defenses, and pulled out.

sentences.zh: 石苞時鎮長安，謀帥關中之眾攻鄴，左長史石光、司馬曹曜等固諫。

translations.literal: Shi Bao at that time was stationed at Chang'an; he plotted to lead the host within the passes to attack Ye; left chief clerk Shi Guang, aide-de-camp Cao Yao, and others firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao, holding Chang'an, plotted to march the Guanzhong armies on Ye; his chief clerk Shi Guang and marshal Cao Yao pleaded in vain against it.

sentences.zh: 苞怒，誅光等百餘人。

translations.literal: Bao was angry and executed Guang and more than one hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao flew into a rage and put Shi Guang and over a hundred men to death.

sentences.zh: 苞性貪而無謀，雍州豪石知其無成，並遣使告晉梁州刺史司馬勳。

translations.literal: Bao by nature was greedy and without stratagem; the magnates of Yongzhou knew he would not succeed and together sent envoys to inform Jin's Liangzhou Governor Sima Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and feckless, Shi Bao convinced Yongzhou notables he would fail; they all sent word to Jin's Liangzhou governor Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳於是率眾赴之，壁於懸鉤，去長安二百餘里，使治中劉煥攻京兆太守劉秀離，斬之。

translations.literal: Xun thereupon led the host to join them, fortified at Xuankou more than two hundred li from Chang'an, and ordered administrator Liu Huan to attack Jingzhao Governor Liu Xiuli, beheading him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xun marched to their aid, walled up at Xuankou within two hundred li of Chang'an, and had Liu Huan storm Jingzhao prefect Liu Xiuli and take his head.

sentences.zh: 三輔豪右多殺其令長，擁三十餘壁，有眾五萬以應勳。

translations.literal: The great families of the three adjuncts mostly killed their magistrates and chiefs, held more than thirty fortresses, and had a host of fifty thousand to answer Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Sanfu grandees slew their magistrates, raised thirty-odd stockades, and rallied fifty thousand men for Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 苞輟攻鄴之謀，使麻秋、姚國等率騎距勳。

translations.literal: Bao dropped the plan to attack Ye and sent Ma Qiu, Yao Guo, and others to lead horse to oppose Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao abandoned the march on Ye and sent Ma Qiu and Yao Guo out with cavalry to meet Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 遵遣車騎王朗率精騎二萬，以外討勳為名，因劫苞，送之於鄴。

translations.literal: Zun sent chariot-and-horse general Wang Lang leading twenty thousand picked horse, in the name of campaigning against Xun, seized Bao by surprise and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun dispatched Wang Lang with twenty thousand elite riders on the pretext of fighting Sima Xun, ambushed Shi Bao, and shipped him to Ye.

sentences.zh: 勳又為朗所距，釋懸鉤，拔宛城，殺遵南陽太守袁景而還。

translations.literal: Xun was again blocked by Lang, released Xuankou, took Wancheng, killed Zun's Nanyang Governor Yuan Jing, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang checked Sima Xun, who lifted the Xuankou camp, seized Wancheng, killed Shi Zun's Nanyang governor Yuan Jing, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，遵之發李城也，謂石閔曰：「努力！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zun set out from Licheng, he said to Shi Min: "Strive hard!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zun left Licheng he had told Shi Min, "Fight your hardest!"

sentences.zh: 事成，以爾為儲貳。

translations.literal: When the affair succeeds, We shall make you heir."
translations.idiomatic: "If this succeeds, you will be my heir."

sentences.zh: 」既而立衍，閔甚失望，自以勳高一時，規專朝政，遵忌而不能任。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he established Yan; Min was greatly disappointed; he deemed his merit highest of the age and plotted to monopolize court governance; Zun envied him and could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Shi Zun enthroned Shi Yan; Shi Min seethed—he thought his feats unmatched and meant to dominate the court, while Shi Zun envied him and gave him no real power.

sentences.zh: 閔既為都督，總內外兵權，乃懷撫殿中將士及故東宮高力萬餘人，皆奏為殿中員外將軍，爵關外侯，賜以宮女，樹己之恩。

translations.literal: Once Min was commander-in-chief and held all military authority within and without, he soothed palace hall officers and former eastern-palace Gao Li more than ten thousand men, all memorialized as supernumerary palace hall generals with noble rank marquis beyond the passes, granted palace women, and planted his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: As commander-in-chief Shi Min won over the palace guard and ten thousand former Gao Li toughs, had them all brevetted hall generals and marquis beyond the passes, showered them with palace ladies, and built a private following.

sentences.zh: 遵弗之猜也，而更題名善惡以挫抑之，眾咸怨矣。

translations.literal: Zun did not suspect this and instead wrote names of good and evil to humiliate them; the host all resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun never saw the danger; he posted blacklists to shame those troops, and the men turned bitter.

sentences.zh: 而又納中書令孟准、左衛將軍王鸞之計，頗疑憚于閔，稍奪兵權。

translations.literal: Moreover he adopted the plan of Palace Secretariat Director Meng Zhun and left guard general Wang Luan, was quite suspicious and fearful of Min, and gradually stripped military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding Meng Zhun and Wang Luan, Shi Zun grew wary of Shi Min and began stripping away his commands.

sentences.zh: 閔益有恨色，准等咸勸誅之。

translations.literal: Min increasingly showed hatred; Zhun and the others all urged executing him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min's scowl deepened, and Meng Zhun urged his murder.

sentences.zh: 遵召石鑒等入，議于其太后鄭氏之前，皆請誅之。

translations.literal: Zun summoned Shi Jian and others to enter and deliberate before his empress dowager Lady Zheng; all requested to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun called Shi Jian and others before Empress Dowager Zheng; every voice called for Shi Min's death.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏曰：「李城回師，無棘奴豈有今日！

translations.literal: Lady Zheng said: "When the army returned from Licheng, without Thorn-the-slave how could there be today!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng answered, "After Licheng, without Thorn-the-slave—Shi Min—where would we be today!"

sentences.zh: 小驕縱之，不可便殺也。

translations.literal: Let him be a little proud; you must not kill him at once."
translations.idiomatic: "Let him swagger a little; do not cut him down yet."

sentences.zh: 」鑒出，遣宦者楊環馳以告閔，閔遂劫李農及右衛王基，密謀廢遵。

translations.literal: " When Jian left, he sent eunuch Yang Huan galloping to inform Min; Min thereupon seized Li Nong and right guard Wang Ji and secretly plotted to depose Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian slipped out and sent the eunuch Yang Huan racing to warn Shi Min, who seized Li Nong and Wang Ji of the right guard and plotted to depose Shi Zun.

sentences.zh: 使將軍蘇亥、周成率甲士三十執遵于如意觀。

translations.literal: He ordered generals Su Hai and Zhou Cheng to lead thirty armored soldiers and seize Zun at the Ruyi Belvedere.
translations.idiomatic: He had Su Hai and Zhou Cheng drag thirty armored men into the Ruyi belvedere and arrest Shi Zun.

sentences.zh: 遵時方與婦人彈棋，問成等曰：「反者誰也？

translations.literal: Zun was at that moment playing pitch-pot with a woman and asked Cheng and the others: "Who rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun was playing pitch-pot with a concubine and asked Zhou Cheng, "Who rises against me?"

sentences.zh: 」成曰：「義陽王鑒當立。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Prince Yiyang Jian ought to be established."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cheng answered, "Prince Yiyang Shi Jian is to be enthroned."

sentences.zh: 」遵曰：「我尚如是，汝等立鑒，復能幾時！

translations.literal: Zun said: "We are still like this; you establish Jian—how long can it last!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun sneered, "If I end like this, how long will you last once you set Shi Jian on the throne!"

sentences.zh: 」乃殺之于琨華殿，誅鄭氏及其太子衍、上光祿張斐、中書令孟准、左衛王鸞等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they killed him at the Kunhua Hall, executed Lady Zheng and his heir apparent Yan, senior shining official Zhang Fei, palace director Meng Zhun, left guard Wang Luan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They slew him in the Kunhua hall, killed Empress Dowager Zheng, crown prince Shi Yan, Zhang Fei, Meng Zhun, Wang Luan, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 遵凡在位一百八十三日。

translations.literal: Zun had altogether occupied the position one hundred eighty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun had ruled a hundred and eighty-three days.

sentences.zh: 石鑒

translations.literal: Shi Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Heading: Shi Jian.

sentences.zh: 鑒乃僭位，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon usurped the throne and granted general amnesty short of capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian seized the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty short of capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 以石閔為大將軍，封武德王，李農為大司馬，並錄尚書事；

translations.literal: He appointed Shi Min as grand general and enfeoffed him prince of Wude, Li Nong as grand marshal, both concurrently recording Masters-of-Writing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He named Shi Min grand general and prince of Wude, Li Nong grand marshal—both with custody of the secretariat;

sentences.zh: 郎闓為司空，秦州刺史劉群為尚書左僕射，侍中盧諶為中書監。

translations.literal: Lang Kan was minister of works; Qinzhou Governor Liu Qun was left vice-director of Masters-of-Writing; attendant Lu Chen was palace secretariat supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Kan became minister of works, Liu Qun of Qinzhou left vice-director of the secretariat, and attendant Lu Chen palace secretariat supervisor.

sentences.zh: 鑒使石苞及中書令李松、殿中將軍張才等夜誅閔、農于琨華殿，不克，禁中擾亂。

translations.literal: Jian sent Shi Bao and palace director Li Song, hall general Zhang Cai, and others by night to execute Min and Nong at Kunhua Hall; they did not succeed; the palace was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian sent Shi Bao, Li Song, hall officer Zhang Cai, and others to murder Shi Min and Li Nong in the Kunhua hall; the strike failed and the palace erupted in chaos.

sentences.zh: 鑒恐閔為變，偽若不知者，夜斬松、才于西中華門，並誅石苞。

translations.literal: Jian feared Min would mutiny and pretended not to know; by night he executed Song and Cai at the western Zhonghua Gate and also executed Shi Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Shi Min's reprisal, Shi Jian feigned ignorance, then had Li Song and Zhang Cai cut down at the western Zhonghua gate and killed Shi Bao as well.

sentences.zh: 時石祗在襄國，與姚弋仲、苻洪等通和，連兵檄誅閔、農。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Zhi was at Xiangguo; with Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, and others he had opened peace and joined forces with proclamations to execute Min and Nong.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shi Zhi at Xiangguo had allied with Yao Yizhong and Fu Hong and issued calls to extirpate Shi Min and Li Nong.

sentences.zh: 鑒遣石琨為大都督，與張舉及侍中呼延盛率步騎七萬分討祗等。

translations.literal: Jian sent Shi Kun as grand commander-in-chief with Zhang Ju and attendant Huyan Sheng leading seventy thousand infantry and horse in separate columns to punish Zhi and the others.
