translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian dispatched Shi Kun as commander-in-chief with Zhang Ju and Huyan Sheng at the head of seventy thousand horse and foot to crush Shi Zhi.

sentences.zh: 中領軍石成、侍中石啟、前河東太守石暉謀誅閔、農，閔、農殺之。

translations.literal: Central garrison general Shi Cheng, attendant Shi Qi, former Hedong prefect Shi Hui plotted to kill Min and Nong; Min and Nong killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cheng, Shi Qi, and former Hedong governor Shi Hui plotted against Shi Min and Li Nong; Shi Min and Li Nong slew them first.

sentences.zh: 龍驤孫伏都、劉銖等結羯士三千伏于胡天，亦欲誅閔等。

translations.literal: Dragon-soaring Sun Fudu and Liu Zhu and others linked three thousand Jie soldiers ambushed at Hutian, also intending to execute Min and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fudu and Liu Zhu mustered three thousand Jie troops in ambush at the Hu field, likewise aiming to kill Shi Min.

sentences.zh: 時鑒在中臺，伏都率三十餘人將升臺挾鑒以攻之。

translations.literal: At that time Jian was on the Central Terrace; Fudu led more than thirty men intending to ascend the terrace and seize Jian to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Jian on the Central Terrace, Sun Fudu tried to rush thirty men up the stairs to seize the emperor as a shield.

sentences.zh: 臨見伏都毀閣道，鑒問其故。

translations.literal: When he drew near and saw Fudu destroying the gallery bridge, Jian asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Sun Fudu tear up the gallery walk, Shi Jian demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 伏都曰：「李農等反，巳在東掖門，臣嚴率衛士，謹先啟知。

translations.literal: Fudu said: "Li Nong and others rebel; they are already at the eastern side gate; your servant strictly leads guards and respectfully reports first."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fudu shouted that Li Nong had mutinied at the eastern side gate of Ye and that he was rallying the guard to inform the throne.

sentences.zh: 」鑒曰：「卿是功臣，好為官陳力。

translations.literal: Jian said: "You are a meritorious subject; exert yourself well for the office."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian said, "You are a trusted champion—serve the office with all you have."

sentences.zh: 朕從臺觀卿，勿慮無報也。

translations.literal: We shall watch you from the terrace; do not worry about lacking reward."
translations.idiomatic: "I shall watch from the tower—serve well and you will be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 」於是伏都及銖率眾攻閔、農，不克，屯于鳳陽門。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Fudu and Zhu led the host to attack Min and Nong; they did not succeed and encamped at Fengyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fudu and Liu Zhu then struck Shi Min and Li Nong, failed, and drew up at Fengyang gate.

sentences.zh: 閔、農率眾數千毀金明門而入。

translations.literal: Min and Nong led several thousand of the host, destroyed the Golden Bright Gate, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min and Li Nong smashed the Golden Bright gate with a few thousand men and forced their way in.

sentences.zh: 鑒懼閔之誅己也，馳招閔、農，開門內之，謂曰：「孫伏都反，卿宜速討之。

translations.literal: Jian feared Min would execute him and urgently summoned Min and Nong, opened the gates to admit them, saying: "Sun Fudu rebels; you ought quickly to punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified that Shi Min would kill him, Shi Jian flung open the gates, welcomed Shi Min and Li Nong, and cried that Sun Fudu had rebelled and must be crushed at once.

sentences.zh: 」閔、農攻斬伏都等，自鳳陽至琨華，橫屍相枕，流血成渠。

translations.literal: Min and Nong attacked and beheaded Fudu and the others; from Fengyang to Kunhua corpses lay pillow to pillow and blood flowed in channels.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min and Li Nong cut down Sun Fudu and his party; from Fengyang to Kunhua the dead lay in heaps and blood ran in ditches.

sentences.zh: 宣令內外六夷敢稱兵杖者斬之。

translations.literal: He proclaimed to inner and outer that any of the six Yi who dared bear arms would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that any non-Han who took up weapons inside or outside the city would die.

sentences.zh: 胡人或斬關，或逾城而出者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Hu persons who cut through gates or climbed walls to go out could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Countless non-Han smashed gates or scaled the walls to flee.

sentences.zh: 使尚書王簡、少府王郁帥眾數千，守鑒於禦龍觀，懸食給之。

translations.literal: He ordered Masters-of-Writing Wang Jian and chamberlain Wang Yu to lead several thousand of the host and guard Jian at the Imperial Dragon Belvedere, suspending food to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wang Jian and Wang Yu pen Shi Jian inside the Imperial Dragon belvedere with a few thousand guards and fed him on lowered baskets.

sentences.zh: 令城內曰：「與官同心者住，不同心者各任所之。

translations.literal: He ordered within the city: "Those of one mind with the officials stay; those not of one mind may each go where they will."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran through Ye: "Whoever stands with the court may stay; whoever does not may leave at will."

sentences.zh: 」敕城門不復相禁。

translations.literal: He ordered the city gates no longer mutually forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The gates were thrown open without further checks.

sentences.zh: 於是趙人百里內悉入城，胡羯去者填門。

translations.literal: Thereupon within one hundred li Zhao people all entered the city; Hu and Jie who departed jammed the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred li every Zhao Chinese crowded into the city while Hu and Jie clogged the gates trying to escape.

sentences.zh: 閔知胡之不為己用也，班令內外趙人，斬一胡首送鳳陽門者，文官進位三等，武職悉拜牙門。

translations.literal: Min knew the Hu would not be used for himself; he issued an order to inner and outer Zhao people that whoever sent one Hu head to Fengyang Gate would have civil officials advanced three grades and military posts all brevetted as yamen commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min, seeing the Hu would never serve him, told the Zhao Chinese to bring a Hu head to Fengyang gate for three civil promotions or a military brevet as yamen captain.

sentences.zh: 一日之中，斬首數萬。

translations.literal: Within one day beheadings numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That day they piled up tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 閔躬率趙人誅諸胡羯，無貴賤男女少長皆斬之，死者二十餘萬，屍諸城外，悉為野犬豺狼所食。

translations.literal: Min personally led Zhao people in executing the various Hu and Jie; without regard to noble or base, male or female, young or old, all were beheaded; the dead exceeded two hundred thousand; corpses were piled outside the walls and all were eaten by wild dogs and jackals.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min himself led Zhao troops in slaughtering every Hu and Jie in sight, high or low, man, woman, or child—more than two hundred thousand corpses heaped outside the walls for dogs and wolves to devour.

sentences.zh: 屯據四方者，所在承閔書誅之，于時高鼻多須至有濫死者半。

translations.literal: Those garrisoning the four quarters, wherever they were, on receiving Min's letters executed them; at that time high-nosed and heavily bearded men up to half died wrongfully.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons across the realm carried out Shi Min's writs; high-nosed, bearded men died by mistake in droves.

sentences.zh: 太宰趙鹿、太尉張舉、中軍張春、光祿石嶽、撫軍石甯、武衛張季及諸公侯、卿、校、龍騰等萬餘人出奔襄國。

translations.literal: Grand steward Zhao Lu, grand commandant Zhang Ju, central army Zhang Chun, shining official Shi Yue, stabilizing army Shi Ning, martial guard Zhang Ji, and the various dukes, marquises, ministers, colonels, Dragon Surge, more than ten thousand men, fled toward Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lu, Zhang Ju, Zhang Chun, Shi Yue, Shi Ning, Zhang Ji, and over ten thousand nobles and Dragon Surge guards bolted for Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 石琨奔據冀州，撫軍張沈屯滏口，張賀度據石瀆，建義段勤據黎陽，甯南楊群屯桑壁，劉國據陽城，段龕據陳留，姚弋仲據混橋，苻洪據枋頭，眾各數萬。

translations.literal: Shi Kun fled to occupy Jizhou; stabilizing army Zhang Shen encamped at Fekou; Zhang Hedu held Shidu; righteous-establishment Duan Qin held Liyang; southern pacification Yang Qun encamped at Sangbi; Liu Guo held Yangcheng; Duan Kan held Chenliu; Yao Yizhong held Hun Bridge; Fu Hong held Fangtou; each host numbered several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun fled into Ji province while Zhang Shen, Zhang Hedu, Duan Qin, Yang Qun, Liu Guo, Duan Kan, Yao Yizhong, and Fu Hong seized chokepoints with hosts of tens of thousands each.

sentences.zh: 王朗、麻秋自長安奔於洛陽。

translations.literal: Wang Lang and Ma Qiu fled from Chang'an to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang and Ma Qiu ran from Chang'an to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 秋承閔書，誅朗部胡千餘。

translations.literal: Qiu on receiving Min's letter executed more than a thousand Hu of Lang's command.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu, obeying Shi Min, slaughtered over a thousand Hu in Wang Lang's ranks.

sentences.zh: 朗奔于襄國。

translations.literal: Lang fled to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang fled toward Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 麻秋率眾奔于苻洪。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu led the host and fled to Fu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu took his army over to Fu Hong.

sentences.zh: 石琨及張舉、王朗率眾七萬伐鄴，石閔率騎千餘，距之城北。

translations.literal: Shi Kun with Zhang Ju and Wang Lang led a host of seventy thousand to attack Ye; Shi Min led more than a thousand horse and opposed them north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun, Zhang Ju, and Wang Lang marched seventy thousand men on Ye; Shi Min met them north of the walls with a thousand riders.

sentences.zh: 閔執兩刃矛，馳騎擊之，皆應鋒摧潰，斬級三千。

translations.literal: Min grasped a double-edged spear, galloped his horse to strike them, and all collapsed at the edge of his blade; beheadings numbered three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min charged with a twin-bladed lance and shattered their line, taking three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 琨等大敗，遂歸於冀州。

translations.literal: Kun and the others were greatly defeated and thereupon returned to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun's host broke and fled back into Ji province.

sentences.zh: 閔與李農率騎三萬討張賀度于石瀆，鑒密遣宦者齎書召張沈等，使承虛襲鄴。

translations.literal: Min with Li Nong led thirty thousand horse to punish Zhang Hedu at Shidu; Jian secretly sent eunuchs bearing letters to summon Zhang Shen and others to take advantage of the emptiness to raid Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min and Li Nong rode thirty thousand horse against Zhang Hedu at Shidu while Shi Jian secretly sent eunuchs urging Zhang Shen to strike an empty Ye.

sentences.zh: 宦者以告閔、農，閔、農馳還，廢鑒殺之，誅季龍孫三十八人，盡殪石氏。

translations.literal: The eunuchs informed Min and Nong; Min and Nong galloped back, deposed Jian and killed him, executed thirty-eight of Jilong's grandsons, and utterly extinguished the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs tipped off Shi Min and Li Nong, who raced back, deposed and killed Shi Jian, slaughtered thirty-eight of Shi Hu's grandsons, and wiped out the Shi house.

sentences.zh: 鑒在位一百三日。

translations.literal: Jian had occupied the position one hundred three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian lasted a hundred and three days on the throne.

sentences.zh: 季龍小男混，將妻妾數人奔京師，敕收付廷尉，俄而斬之于建康市。

translations.literal: Jilong's youngest son Hun led wife and concubines several persons fleeing to the capital; an edict ordered him seized and delivered to the commandant of justice; before long he was beheaded at the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's youngest boy Shi Hun fled toward Jin with his women; the court had him jailed and soon beheaded him in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 季龍十三子，五人為冉閔所殺，八人自相殘害，混至此又死。

translations.literal: Jilong had thirteen sons; five were killed by Ran Min; eight mutually slaughtered one another; Hun reaching this point again died.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shi Hu's thirteen sons, Ran Min killed five and eight destroyed one another; Shi Hun's capture ended the line.

sentences.zh: 初，讖言滅石者陵，尋而石閔徙蘭陵公，季龍惡之，改蘭陵為武興郡，至是終為閔所滅。

translations.literal: Earlier a prophecy said "Shi would be destroyed by Ling"; soon Shi Min was moved to be duke of Lanling; Jilong hated it and changed Lanling to Wuxing commandery; reaching this point he was finally destroyed by Min.
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy had said the character ling would doom the house of Shi; when Shi Min became duke of Lan-ling, Shi Hu renamed the commandery to dodge the omen—yet Ran Min still ended the Zhao line.

sentences.zh: 始勒以成帝僭立，二主四子，凡二十三年，以穆帝滅。

translations.literal: At first Le had usurped the throne in Emperor Cheng's time; two rulers and four sons, altogether twenty-three years, ending in Emperor Mu's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: From Shi Le's seizure under Emperor Cheng through two rulers and four princes, twenty-three years passed before Emperor Mu wiped out the line.

sentences.zh: 石閔

translations.literal: Shi Min.
translations.idiomatic: Heading: Shi Min.

sentences.zh: 〈冉閔〉

translations.literal: 〈Ran Min〉
translations.idiomatic: Alternate name: Ran Min.

sentences.zh: 閔字永曾，小字棘奴，季龍之養孫也。

translations.literal: Min's style was Yongzeng; childhood name Thorn-the-slave; he was Jilong's adopted grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min, styled Yongzeng and nicknamed Thorn-the-slave, was Shi Hu's adopted grandson.

sentences.zh: 父瞻，字弘武，本姓冉，名良，魏郡內黃人也。

translations.literal: His father Zhan, style Hongwu, originally surnamed Ran, given name Liang, was a man of Neihuang in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ran Zhan, styled Hongwu—originally Ran Liang of Neihuang in Wei commandery—came from a line of Han Liyang cavalry officers.

sentences.zh: 其先漢黎陽騎都督，累世牙門。

translations.literal: His ancestors were Han Liyang mounted commandants for generation after generation holding yamen posts.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his forebears had served as Han mounted commanders and yamen captains.

sentences.zh: 勒破陳午，獲瞻，時年十二，命季龍子之。

translations.literal: When Le broke Chen Wu, he captured Zhan; at the time he was twelve years old; he ordered Jilong to treat him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le seized him at twelve when Chen Wu fell and told Shi Hu to adopt the boy.

sentences.zh: 驍猛多力，攻戰無前。

translations.literal: He was fierce and brave and strong of force; in attack and battle there was none before him.
translations.idiomatic: He grew fearless and immensely strong, always first in the charge.

sentences.zh: 歷位左積射將軍、西華侯。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to left stacked-shoot general and marquis of Xihua.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left stacked-shoot general and marquis of Xihua.

sentences.zh: 閔幼而果銳，季龍撫之如孫。

translations.literal: Min from youth was decisive and sharp; Jilong reared him like a grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was fierce and keen, and Shi Hu doted on him like a grandson.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長八尺，善謀策，勇力絕人。

translations.literal: When grown, his body was eight chi tall; he was skilled in stratagem; courage and strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to eight chi, he was cunning in counsel and unmatched in valor.

sentences.zh: 拜建節將軍，徙封修成侯，歷位北中郎將、遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who establishes the standard, moved enfeoffment to marquis of Xiucheng, and rose through posts to north gentleman-general and raiding general.
translations.idiomatic: He became general who establishes the standard, moved to marquis of Xiucheng, then northern gentleman-general and raiding general.

sentences.zh: 季龍之敗于昌黎，閔軍獨全，由此功名大顯。

translations.literal: When Jilong was defeated at Changli, Min's army alone remained intact; by this his merit and name were greatly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: At Changli, when Shi Hu lost, only Shi Min's corps came out whole, and his fame exploded.

sentences.zh: 及敗梁犢之後，威聲彌振，胡夏宿將莫不憚之。

translations.literal: After defeating Liang Du, his awesome name spread still more; Hu and Xia veteran generals none did not fear him.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang Du's defeat his prestige terrified every Hu and Chinese veteran in the army.

sentences.zh: ，殺石鑒，其司徒申鐘、司空郎闓等四十八人上尊號于閔，閔固讓李農，農以死固請，於是僭即皇帝位於南郊，大赦，改元曰永興，國號大魏，復姓冉氏。

translations.literal: Having killed Shi Jian, his minister of works Shen Zhong, minister of works Lang Kan, and forty-eight others offered Min the elevated title; Min firmly yielded to Li Nong; Nong with death firmly urged; thereupon he usurped the emperor's position at the southern suburb, granted general amnesty, changed the era name to Yongxing, state title Great Wei, and restored the surname Ran.
translations.idiomatic: After executing Shi Jian, Shen Zhong, Lang Kan, and forty-eight others urged the throne on him; Shi Min pressed the honor on Li Nong until Li Nong begged with his life; then Shi Min took the title at the southern altar, declared Yongxing, named the state Great Wei, and resumed the surname Ran.

sentences.zh: 追尊其祖隆元皇帝，考瞻烈祖高皇帝，尊母王氏為皇太后，立妻董氏為皇后，子智為皇太子。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his grandfather as Emperor Yuan of Long, his father Zhan as Emperor Gaoliezu, honored his mother Lady Wang as empress dowager, established his wife Lady Dong as empress, and his son Zhi as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized his grandfather as Emperor Yuan, his father Ran Zhan as Emperor Liegao, raised Lady Wang to empress dowager, Lady Dong to empress, and named his son Ran Zhi crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以李農為太宰、領太尉、錄尚書事，封齊王，農諸子皆封為縣公。

translations.literal: He appointed Li Nong grand steward, concurrently grand commandant, recording Masters-of-Writing affairs, enfeoffed prince of Qi; Nong's various sons were all enfeoffed county dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong became grand steward, grand marshal, and secretariat regent with the title prince of Qi; each of his sons received a county duchy.

sentences.zh: 封其子胤、明、裕皆為王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his sons Yin, Ming, and Yu all as princes.
translations.idiomatic: He made his sons Ran Yin, Ran Ming, and Ran Yu princes in turn.

sentences.zh: 文武進位三等，封爵有差。

translations.literal: Civil and military advanced three grades; noble enfeoffments differed.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers gained three steps in rank and graded noble titles.

sentences.zh: 遣使者持節赦諸屯結，皆不從。

translations.literal: He sent envoys bearing staffs of office to pardon the various encamped hosts; none obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys with imperial batons offered pardons to every rebel camp—and every camp refused.

sentences.zh: 石祗聞鑒死，僭稱尊號于襄國，諸六夷據州郡擁兵者皆應之。

translations.literal: When Shi Zhi heard Jian was dead, he usurped the supreme title at Xiangguo; all six Yi who held prefectures and commands with troops answered him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi at Xiangguo claimed the imperial style, and every non-Han warlord with a garrison rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 閔遣使臨江告晉曰：「胡逆亂中原，今已誅之。

translations.literal: Min sent an envoy to the river to inform Jin, saying: "The Hu have rebelled in the central plain; now We have executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min sent a herald across the river to Jin: "The Hu have torn the heartland apart; I have put them to the sword."

sentences.zh: 若能共討者，可遣軍來也。

translations.literal: If you can jointly punish them, you may dispatch troops."
translations.idiomatic: "If you wish to finish the work, send your armies."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不答。

translations.literal: " The court did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 閔誅李農及其三子，並尚書令王謨、侍中王衍、中常侍嚴震、趙升等。

translations.literal: Min executed Li Nong and his three sons together with Masters-of-Writing Director Wang Mo, attendant Wang Yan, palace attendant Yan Zhen, Zhao Sheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min then killed Li Nong and his three sons along with Wang Mo, Wang Yan, Yan Zhen, Zhao Sheng, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 晉盧江太守袁真攻其合肥，執南蠻校尉桑坦，遷其百姓而還。

translations.literal: Jin's Lujiang Governor Yuan Zhen attacked their Hefei, captured southern Man colonel Sang Tan, relocated the common people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Lujiang governor Yuan Zhen struck Hefei, took southern Man colonel Sang Tan captive, and marched the population away.

sentences.zh: 石祗遣其相國石琨率眾十萬伐鄴，進據邯鄲。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi sent his chancellor Shi Kun leading a host of one hundred thousand to attack Ye and advanced to occupy Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi dispatched his chancellor Shi Kun with a hundred thousand troops against Ye and seized Handan.

sentences.zh: 祗鎮南劉國自繁陽會琨。

translations.literal: Zhi's southern stabilizer Liu Guo joined Kun from Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi's southern commander Liu Guo marched from Fanyang to join Shi Kun.

sentences.zh: 閔大敗琨于邯鄲，死者萬餘。

translations.literal: Min greatly defeated Kun at Handan; the dead exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min shattered Shi Kun at Handan, leaving more than ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 劉國還屯繁陽。

translations.literal: Liu Guo returned to encamp at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guo withdrew to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 苻健自枋頭入關。

translations.literal: Fu Jian entered the passes from Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian led his host from Fangtou into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 張賀度、段勤與劉國、靳豚會於昌城，將攻鄴。

translations.literal: Zhang Hedu, Duan Qin, Liu Guo, and Jin Tun met at Changcheng and were about to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hedu, Duan Qin, Liu Guo, and Jin Tun rendezvoused at Changcheng to strike Ye.

sentences.zh: 閔遣尚書左僕射劉群為行臺都督，使其將王泰、崔通、周成等帥步騎十二萬次於黃城，閔躬統精卒八萬繼之，戰於蒼亭。

translations.literal: Min sent left vice-director of Masters-of-Writing Liu Qun as mobile headquarters commander-in-chief, ordered his generals Wang Tai, Cui Tong, Zhou Cheng, and others to lead one hundred twenty thousand infantry and horse and halt at Huangcheng; Min personally commanded eighty thousand picked troops following them and fought at Cangting.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min made Liu Qun field commander and sent Wang Tai, Cui Tong, and Zhou Cheng with a hundred and twenty thousand troops to Huangcheng, then followed with eighty thousand picked men and met the allies at Cangting.

sentences.zh: 賀度等大敗，死者二萬八千，追斬勒豚于陰安鄉，盡俘其眾，振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Hedu and the others were greatly defeated; the dead numbered twenty-eight thousand; they pursued and beheaded Jin Tun at Yin'an township, captured all his host, and returned with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hedu was routed with twenty-eight thousand slain; Ran Min ran down Jin Tun at Yin'an, took the whole army captive, and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 戎卒三十餘萬，旌旗鐘鼓綿亙百餘里，雖石氏之盛無以過之。

translations.literal: Field troops exceeded three hundred thousand; banners, bells, and drums stretched more than one hundred li; even at the height of the Shi house it did not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Over three hundred thousand soldiers, banners and drums strung a hundred li—greater pomp than the Shi ever mustered.

sentences.zh: 閔至自蒼亭，行飲至之禮，清定九流，准才授任，儒學後門多蒙顯進，于時翕然，方之為魏晉之初。

translations.literal: When Min returned from Cangting he held the victory feast, clarified and fixed the nine ranks, granted office according to talent; many rear-gate scholars of Confucian learning received splendid advancement; at the time all agreed it resembled the early Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Back from Cangting he held the victory rites, sorted the nine grades, matched posts to talent, and promoted humble scholars until men said it felt like the early Wei-Jin renewal.

sentences.zh: 閔率步騎十萬攻石祗于襄國，署其子太原王胤為大單于、驃騎大將軍，以降胡一千配為麾下。

translations.literal: Min led one hundred thousand infantry and horse to attack Shi Zhi at Xiangguo, appointed his son Prince of Taiyuan Yin as grand shanyu and general of agile cavalry, and assigned one thousand surrendered Hu to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min marched a hundred thousand on Xiangguo, named his son Ran Yin grand shanyu and swift-cavalry general, and gave him a thousand Hu auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫韋謏啟諫甚切，閔覽之大怒，誅謏及其子孫。

translations.literal: Shining official Wei Xian remonstrated urgently; when Min read it he was greatly angry and executed Xian together with his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xian remonstrated bluntly; Ran Min read the memorial, flew into a rage, and exterminated his line.

sentences.zh: 閔攻襄國百餘日，為土山地道，築室反耕。

translations.literal: Min attacked Xiangguo more than one hundred days, built earthen hills and tunnels, raised huts and reverse-plowed.
translations.idiomatic: For over a hundred days he besieged Xiangguo with siege mounds, saps, huts on the lines, and trench farming.

sentences.zh: 祗大懼，去皇帝之號，稱趙王，遣使詣慕容俊、姚弋仲以乞師。

translations.literal: Zhi was greatly afraid, removed the emperor's title, styled himself king of Zhao, and sent envoys to Murong Jun and Yao Yizhong to beg troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi panicked, dropped the imperial title for "king of Zhao," and begged Murong Jun and Yao Yizhong for relief.

sentences.zh: 會石琨自冀州援祗，弋仲復遣其子襄率騎三萬八千至自滆頭，俊遣將軍悅綰率甲卒三萬自龍城，三方勁卒合十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Shi Kun came from Jizhou to aid Zhi, Yizhong again sent his son Xiang leading thirty-eight thousand horse from Pitou; Jun sent general Yue Wan leading thirty thousand armored troops from Longcheng; the three sides' crack troops together exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun marched from Ji to help while Yao Xiang brought thirty-eight thousand riders from Pitou and Murong Jun sent Yue Wan with thirty thousand from Longcheng—well over a hundred thousand converged on the siege.

sentences.zh: 閔遣車騎胡睦距襄下場長蘆，將軍孫威候琨于黃丘，皆為敵所敗，士卒略盡，睦、威單騎而還。

translations.literal: Min sent chariot-and-horse Hu Mu to oppose Xiang at Changlu below the field; general Sun Wei awaited Kun at Huangqiu; all were defeated by the enemy; soldiers were nearly exhausted; Mu and Wei returned alone on horse.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min sent Hu Mu and Sun Wei to block Yao Xiang and Shi Kun; both lines collapsed, and the generals fled back alone.

sentences.zh: 琨等軍且至，閔將出擊之，衛將軍王泰諫曰：「窮寇固迷，希望外援。

translations.literal: As Kun and the others' army was about to arrive, Min was about to go out to strike them; guard general Wang Tai remonstrated, saying: "A cornered band is surely deluded and hopes for outside relief.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the allied arrival Wang Tai urged, "Besieged foes cling to delusions and wait on rescuers."

sentences.zh: 今強救雲集，欲吾出戰，腹背擊我。

translations.literal: Now strong rescuers gather like clouds; they desire Us to go out and fight so they may strike Us front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Their reinforcements want you to sortie so they can hit you front and rear."

sentences.zh: 宜固壘勿出，觀勢而動，以挫其謀。

translations.literal: It is fitting to hold the ramparts and not go out, watch the situation and move, to thwart their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the walls, watch how the wind shifts, and break their plan."

sentences.zh: 今陛下親戎，如失萬全，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Now if Your Majesty personally takes the army and should miss perfect completeness, the great affair is gone.
translations.idiomatic: If you ride out yourself and anything goes wrong, the cause is lost."

sentences.zh: 請慎無出，臣請率諸將為陛下滅之。

translations.literal: We beg you be careful and not go out; your servant begs to lead the various generals to destroy them for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Stay inside, my lord—give me the command and I will wipe them out for you."

sentences.zh: 」閔將從之，道士法饒進曰：「太白經昴，當殺胡王，一戰百克，不可失也。

translations.literal: " Min was about to follow this when Daoist Fa Rao advanced, saying: "The White Planet crosses Mao; it ought to slay the Hu king; one battle brings a hundred victories; it must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min almost agreed until the Daoist Fa Rao cried that Venus crossing Mao meant the Hu king would fall and one stroke would win all—do not miss the omen."

sentences.zh: 」閔攘袂大言曰：「吾戰決矣，敢諫者斬！

translations.literal: " Min rolled up his sleeves and declared greatly: "Our battle is decided; whoever dares remonstrate will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min flung back his sleeves and roared, "I fight—whoever counsels retreat dies!"

sentences.zh: 」於是盡眾出戰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he brought out the entire host to battle.
translations.idiomatic: He then hurled every man into the field.

sentences.zh: 姚襄、悅綰、石琨等三面攻之，祗沖其後，閔師大敗。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang, Yue Wan, Shi Kun, and others attacked him on three sides; Zhi struck his rear; Min's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang, Yue Wan, and Shi Kun closed on three sides while Shi Zhi rammed the rear—Ran Min's army broke.

sentences.zh: 閔潛于襄國行宮，與十餘騎奔鄴。

translations.literal: Min hid in the Xiangguo traveling palace and with more than ten riders fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min slipped into the field palace, then galloped to Ye with a dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 降胡栗特康等執冉胤及左僕射劉琦等送於祗，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Surrendered Hu Lute Kang and others seized Ran Yin and left vice-director Liu Qi and others and sent them to Zhi, who killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Hu turncoats seized Ran Yin and Liu Qi and handed them to Shi Zhi, who executed them.

sentences.zh: 司空石璞、尚書令徐機、車騎胡睦、侍中李琳、中書監盧諶、少府王郁、尚書劉欽、劉休等諸將士死者十餘萬人，於是人物殲矣。

translations.literal: Minister of works Shi Pu, Masters-of-Writing Director Xu Ji, chariot-and-horse Hu Mu, attendant Li Lin, palace secretariat supervisor Lu Chen, chamberlain Wang Yu, Masters-of-Writing Liu Qin, Liu Xiu, and other generals and officers who died exceeded one hundred thousand persons; at this point the notables were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, Xu Ji, Hu Mu, Lu Chen, Wang Yu, Liu Qin, and more than a hundred thousand officers perished—Zhao's elite was gone.

sentences.zh: 賊盜蜂起，司、冀大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: Bandits swarmed like bees; Si and Ji suffered great famine; people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Brigands erupted across Si and Ji in a famine so grim that men ate men.

sentences.zh: 自季龍末年而閔盡散倉庫以樹私恩。

translations.literal: From Jilong's closing years Min had utterly scattered the granaries to plant private kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shi Hu's last years Ran Min had emptied the granaries to buy loyalty.

sentences.zh: 與羌胡相攻，無月不戰。

translations.literal: He attacked Qiang and Hu without a month without battle.
translations.idiomatic: He warred against Qiang and Hu without pause.

sentences.zh: 青、雍、幽、荊州徙戶及諸氐、羌、胡、蠻數百餘萬，各還本土，道路交錯，互相殺掠，且饑疫死亡，其能達者十有二三。

translations.literal: More than several million relocated households of Qing, Yong, You, Jing provinces and the various Di, Qiang, Hu, and Man each returned to native soil; roads crossed and they mutually killed and plundered; moreover famine and pestilence killed them; of those who could reach perhaps two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Millions driven from Qing, Yong, You, and Jing—Di, Qiang, Hu, and Man alike—clogged the roads homeward, slaughtering each other until famine and plague left only two or three in ten alive.

sentences.zh: 諸夏紛亂，無復農者。

translations.literal: The central Xia were thrown into chaos; there were no longer farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Heartland China fell so chaotic that no one farmed.

sentences.zh: 閔悔之，誅法饒父子，支解之，贈韋謏大司徒。

translations.literal: Min regretted it, executed Fa Rao and his sons, dismembered them, and posthumously honored Wei Xian as grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min repented, drew and quartered Fa Rao's family, and posthumously ennobled Wei Xian.

sentences.zh: 石祗使劉顯帥眾七萬攻鄴。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi sent Liu Xian leading seventy thousand to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi ordered Liu Xian against Ye with seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時閔潛還，莫有知者，內外凶凶，皆謂閔已沒矣。

translations.literal: At that time Min had secretly returned; none knew; inner and outer were terrified; all said Min had already perished.
translations.idiomatic: None knew Ran Min had slipped back; the capital whispered he was dead.

sentences.zh: 射聲校尉張艾勸閔親郊，以安眾心，閔從之，訛言乃止。

translations.literal: Archer captain Zhang Ai urged Min personally to sacrifice in the suburbs to calm the host's hearts; Min followed this and the false rumors then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ai persuaded him to ride out to a suburban sacrifice to steady morale, and the panic rumors died.

sentences.zh: 劉顯次於明光宮，去鄴二十三里，閔懼，召衛將軍王泰議之。

translations.literal: Liu Xian halted at Mingguang Palace twenty-three li from Ye; Min feared and summoned guard general Wang Tai to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian camped at Mingguang, twenty-three li from Ye; Ran Min panicked and called in Wang Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰恚其謀之不從，辭以瘡甚。

translations.literal: Tai resented that his plan had not been followed and declined on the grounds that his sores were severe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tai, still bitter that his advice had been ignored, pleaded a running sore.

sentences.zh: 閔親臨問之，固稱疾篤。

translations.literal: Min personally came to ask him; he firmly claimed grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min visited his sickbed, but Wang Tai insisted he was dying.

sentences.zh: 閔怒，還宮，顧謂左右曰：「巴奴，乃公豈假汝為命邪！

translations.literal: Min was angry, returned to the palace, turned to those at his side and said: "Ba slave—does Our old man borrow your life!"
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Ran Min snarled to his attendants, "That Ba lout thinks I need his breath to live!"

sentences.zh: 要將先滅群胡，卻斬王泰。

translations.literal: We intend first to destroy the mass of Hu, then behead Wang Tai."
translations.idiomatic: "I'll butcher the Hu first, then take Wang Tai's head."

sentences.zh: 」於是盡眾而戰，大敗顯軍，追奔及于陽平，斬首三萬餘級。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he brought out the entire host to fight, greatly defeated Xian's army, pursued to Yangping, and beheaded more than thirty thousand levels.
translations.idiomatic: He threw the whole army at Liu Xian, routed him, ran him down to Yangping, and took thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 顯懼，密使請降，求殺祗為效，閔振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Xian feared, secretly sent requesting surrender, begged to kill Zhi as proof of merit; Min returned with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian offered to kill Shi Zhi to buy peace; Ran Min marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 會有告王泰招集秦人，將奔關中，閔怒，誅泰，夷其三族。

translations.literal: When someone reported Wang Tai was gathering Qin people planning to flee to the passes within, Min was angry and executed Tai and exterminated his three clans.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Wang Tai was recruiting Qin men to bolt for Guanzhong, Ran Min executed him and extirpated three kinships.

sentences.zh: 劉顯果殺祗及其太宰趙鹿等十餘人，傳首於鄴，送質請命。

translations.literal: Liu Xian indeed killed Zhi together with his grand steward Zhao Lu and more than ten others, sent the heads to Ye, and sent hostages begging for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian did murder Shi Zhi, Zhao Lu, and a dozen others, boxed their heads to Ye, and sent hostages to sue for mercy.

sentences.zh: 驃騎石甯奔于柏人。

translations.literal: Agile-cavalry Shi Ning fled to Bairen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning, swift-cavalry general, fled to Bairen.

sentences.zh: 閔命焚祗首於通衢。

translations.literal: Min ordered Zhi's head burned at the crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min had Shi Zhi's head burned at a public crossroads.

sentences.zh: 閔徐州刺史劉啟以鄄城歸順。

translations.literal: Min's Xuzhou governor Liu Qi brought Juancheng to allegiance in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's Xuzhou governor Liu Qi handed Juancheng to Jin.

sentences.zh: 劉顯復率眾伐鄴，閔擊敗之。

translations.literal: Liu Xian again led the host to attack Ye; Min struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian struck Ye again and was beaten once more.

sentences.zh: 還，稱號于襄國。

translations.literal: He returned and assumed title at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He retreated to Xiangguo and proclaimed himself ruler there.

sentences.zh: 閔徐州刺史周成、兗州刺史魏統、豫州牧冉遇、荊州刺史樂弘皆以城歸順。

translations.literal: Min's Xuzhou governor Zhou Cheng, Yanzhou governor Wei Tong, Yuzhou shepherd Ran Yu, Jingzhou governor Yue Hong all brought their cities to allegiance in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cheng, Wei Tong, Ran Yu, and Yue Hong each surrendered their provinces to Jin.

sentences.zh: 平南高崇、征虜呂護執洛州刺史鄭系，以三河歸順。

translations.literal: Southern pacification Gao Chong and captive-quelling Lu Hu seized Luozhou governor Zheng Xi and brought the three He region to allegiance in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chong and Lu Hu seized Luoyang's Zheng Xi and delivered the three He districts to Jin.

sentences.zh: 慕容彪攻陷中山，殺閔甯北白同、幽州刺史劉准，降于慕容俊。

translations.literal: Murong Biao stormed and took Zhongshan, killed Min's northern stabilizer Bai Tong and Youzhou governor Liu Zhun, and surrendered to Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Biao took Zhongshan, killed Ran Min's northern commander Bai Tong and Youzhou's Liu Zhun, and went over to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 時有雲黃赤色，起東北，長百餘丈，一白鳥從雲間西南去，占者惡之。

translations.literal: At that time there was cloud of yellow-red color rising in the northeast, more than one hundred zhang long; a white bird went from within the cloud southwest; diviners hated it.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-zhang saffron cloud boiled up in the northeast and a white bird cut southwest through it—omen-readers shuddered.

sentences.zh: 劉顯率眾伐常山，太守蘇亥告難於閔。

translations.literal: Liu Xian led the host to attack Changshan; prefect Su Hai reported distress to Min.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian marched on Changshan; Su Hai begged Ran Min for rescue.

sentences.zh: 閔留其大將軍蔣幹等輔其太子智守鄴，親率騎八千救之。

translations.literal: Min left his grand general Jiang Gan and others to assist his heir apparent Zhi in guarding Ye; he personally led eight thousand horse to save them.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min left Jiang Gan to hold Ye with crown prince Ran Zhi and rode eight thousand cavalry to the relief.

sentences.zh: 顯所署大司馬、清河王甯以棗強降于閔，收其餘眾，擊顯，敗之，追奔及于襄國。

translations.literal: The grand marshal Prince of Qinghe Ning whom Xian had appointed brought Zaqiang to surrender to Min; he gathered the remaining host, struck Xian, defeated him, and pursued to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian's grand marshal, Prince Qinghe, came over at Zaqiang; Ran Min rallied the rest, shattered Liu Xian, and chased him to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 顯大將曹伏駒開門為應，遂入襄國，誅顯及其公卿已下百餘人，焚襄國宮室，遷其百姓于鄴。

translations.literal: Xian's great general Cao Fuju opened the gates as inside response; thereupon they entered Xiangguo, executed Xian and more than one hundred of his dukes and ministers downward, burned Xiangguo palace halls, and moved the common people to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fuju opened Xiangguo's gates; Ran Min slew Liu Xian and his court, torched the palace, and marched the people to Ye.

sentences.zh: 顯領軍范路率眾千餘，斬關奔於枋頭。

translations.literal: Xian's central army Fan Lu led more than a thousand of the host, cut through the barrier, and fled to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Lu hacked through the gates with a thousand men and bolted for Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 時慕容俊已克幽、薊，略地至於冀州。

translations.literal: At that time Murong Jun had already taken You and Ji and raided territory reaching Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then Murong Jun held You and Ji and was sweeping into Ji province.

sentences.zh: 閔帥騎距之，與慕容恪相遇于魏昌城。

translations.literal: Min led horse to oppose him and met Murong Ke at Weichang city.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min rode out and met Murong Ke at Weichang.

sentences.zh: 閔大將軍董閏、車騎張溫言于閔曰：「鮮卑乘勝氣勁，不可當也，請避之以溢其氣，然後濟師以擊之，可以捷也。

translations.literal: Min's grand general Dong Run and chariot-and-horse Zhang Wen spoke to Min, saying: "The Xianbei ride victory and their vigor is keen; they cannot be opposed; We beg to avoid them to overflow their vigor, then cross the army to strike them and can be victorious."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Run and Zhang Wen urged, "The Xianbei are riding high—pull back, bleed their momentum, then strike."

sentences.zh: 」閔怒曰：「吾成師以出，將平幽州，斬慕容雋。

translations.literal: " Min was angry and said: "We complete the army and go out intending to pacify Youzhou and behead Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min thundered, "I march to pacify Youzhou and behead Murong Jun."

sentences.zh: 今遇恪而避之，人將侮我矣。

translations.literal: Now meeting Ke and avoiding them, people will despise Us."
translations.idiomatic: "If I shy from Murong Ke, the world will mock me."

sentences.zh: 」乃與恪遇，十戰皆敗之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he met Ke and ten battles all defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He closed with Murong Ke and won ten straight clashes—or so he thought.

sentences.zh: 恪乃以鐵鎖連馬，簡善射鮮卑勇而無剛者五千，方陣而前。

translations.literal: Ke thereupon linked horses with iron chains, selected five thousand Xianbei skilled at archery brave but without stubbornness, and advanced in square formation.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke chained his cavalry, picked five thousand Xianbei bowmen, and advanced in a iron-square.

sentences.zh: 閔所乘赤馬曰硃龍，日行千里，左杖雙刃矛，右執鉤戟，順風擊之，斬鮮卑三百餘級。

translations.literal: The red horse Min rode was called Vermilion Dragon; it went one thousand li a day; in his left he grasped a double-edged spear, in his right he held a hook halberd; striking with the wind he beheaded more than three hundred Xianbei levels.
translations.idiomatic: On his crimson charger Vermilion Dragon he bore twin lances and a hook halberd, carving through three hundred Xianbei in one rush.

sentences.zh: 俄而燕騎大至，圍之數周。

translations.literal: Before long Yan horse arrived in great numbers and surrounded them several circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yan cavalry swarmed in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 閔眾寡不敵，躍馬潰圍東走，行二十餘里，馬無故而死，為恪所擒，及董閏、張溫等送之於薊。

translations.literal: Min's host being few could not match the enemy; he leaped his horse, broke the encirclement, and fled east; having gone more than twenty li, the horse for no reason died, and he was captured by Ke; together with Dong Run, Zhang Wen, and others they sent him to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Ran Min punched through the ring and fled twenty li until his horse dropped; Murong Ke took him alive with Dong Run and Zhang Wen and sent them to Ji.

sentences.zh: 俊立閔而問之曰：「汝奴僕下才，何自妄稱天子？

translations.literal: Jun had Min stand and asked him, saying: "You slave and servant petty talent—how dare you usurp the title Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun had him bound and sneered, "A slave-born upstart—what right had you to call yourself emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」閔曰：「天下大亂，爾曹夷狄，人面獸心，尚欲篡逆。

translations.literal: Min said: "All-under-Heaven is in great chaos; you creatures of the Yi-Di, human-faced beast-hearted, still wish to usurp and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min shot back, "The realm is chaos and you barbarians, human-faced beasts, still dream of stealing the throne."

sentences.zh: 我一時英雄，何為不可作帝王邪！

translations.literal: We for a time are heroes—why may We not become emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: "I am a hero of the age—why should I not rule!"

sentences.zh: 」俊怒，鞭之三百，送于龍城，告廆、皝廟。

translations.literal: " Jun was angry, whipped him three hundred strokes, and sent him to Longcheng, reporting to the temples of Hui and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun had him flogged three hundred times and dragged to Longcheng to answer before the shrines of Murong Hui and Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 遣慕容評率眾圍鄴。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Ping leading the host to besiege Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Ping to invest Ye.

sentences.zh: 劉甯及弟崇帥胡騎三千奔于晉陽，蘇亥棄常山奔於新興。

translations.literal: Liu Ning and younger brother Chong led three thousand Hu horse and fled to Jinyang; Su Hai abandoned Changshan and fled to Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning and Liu Chong bolted to Jinyang with three thousand Hu cavalry; Su Hai abandoned Changshan for Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 鄴中饑，人相食，季龍時宮人被食略盡。

translations.literal: Within Ye there was famine; people ate one another; Jilong's time palace women were eaten nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Ye starved into cannibalism until Shi Hu's palace women were devoured almost to the last.

sentences.zh: 冉智尚幼，蔣幹遣侍中繆嵩、詹事劉猗奉表歸順，且乞師于晉。

translations.literal: Ran Zhi was still young; Jiang Gan sent attendant Mi Song and household steward Liu Yi to present a memorial returning to allegiance and moreover to beg troops from Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Young Ran Zhi remained while Jiang Gan sent Mi Song and Liu Yi to Jin with a pledge of submission and a plea for rescue.

sentences.zh: 濮陽太守戴施自倉垣次於棘津，止猗，不聽進，責其傳國璽。

translations.literal: Puyang governor Dai Shi from Cangyuan halted at Jijin, stopped Yi, would not let him advance, and demanded his transmission seal.
translations.idiomatic: Puyang's Dai Shi blocked Liu Yi at Jijin and demanded the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 猗使嵩還鄴復命，幹沈吟未決，施乃率壯士百餘人入鄴，助守三臺，譎之曰：「且出璽付我。

translations.literal: Yi sent Song back to Ye to report; Gan hesitated undecided; Shi then led more than one hundred stout fellows into Ye, assisted in guarding the three terraces, and deceived him, saying: "For the moment hand the seal to Us.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi slipped a hundred braves into Ye, helped man the three towers, and coaxed Jiang Gan, "Lend me the seal for safekeeping."

sentences.zh: 今凶寇在外，道路不通，未敢送也。

translations.literal: Now the fierce bandits are without; roads are not open; We do not dare send it.
translations.idiomatic: "The foe still ring the walls and the roads are cut—I dare not send it south yet."

sentences.zh: 須得璽，當馳白天子耳。

translations.literal: When We obtain the seal, We shall gallop and report to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "Once it is in my hands I will speed word to the Jin court."

sentences.zh: 天子聞璽已在吾處，信卿至誠，必遣軍糧厚相救餉。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven hears the seal is already with Us, he will trust your utmost sincerity and is sure to dispatch army grain to save and supply you thickly."
translations.idiomatic: "When the emperor knows I hold the seal he will trust your good faith and flood you with grain."

sentences.zh: 」幹以為然，乃出璽付之。

translations.literal: " Gan thought it right and thereupon handed out the seal to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gan believed him and surrendered the seal.

sentences.zh: 施宣言使督護何融迎糧，陰令懷璽送于京師。

translations.literal: Shi publicly ordered supervisor-protector He Rong to welcome grain but secretly ordered him to conceal the seal and send it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi announced he was fetching supplies but told He Rong to spirit the seal to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉馬願、龍驤田香開門降評。

translations.literal: Chief of the extended-ranks Ma Yuan and dragon-soaring Tian Xiang opened the gates and surrendered to Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan and Tian Xiang opened Ye's gates to Murong Ping.

sentences.zh: 施、融、蔣幹懸縋而下，奔於倉垣。

translations.literal: Shi, Rong, and Jiang Gan were lowered by ropes and fled to Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi, He Rong, and Jiang Gan slid down ropes and ran to Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 評送閔妻董氏、太子智、太尉申鐘、司空條攸、中書監聶熊，司隸校尉籍羆、中書令李垣及諸王公卿士于薊。

translations.literal: Murong Ping sent Min's wife Lady Dong, heir apparent Zhi, grand commandant Shen Zhong, minister of works Tiao You, palace secretariat Nie Xiong, metropolitan governor Ji Pi, palace director Li Yuan, and the various princes, dukes, ministers, and gentlemen to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping sent Lady Dong, Ran Zhi, Shen Zhong, Tiao You, Nie Xiong, Ji Pi, Li Yuan, and the whole court north to Ji.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王簡、左僕射張乾、右僕射郎肅自殺。

translations.literal: Masters-of-Writing Director Wang Jian, left vice-director Zhang Qian, right vice-director Lang Su killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Zhang Qian, and Lang Su took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 俊送閔既至龍城，斬於遏陘山。

translations.literal: When Jun had sent Min to Longcheng, he beheaded him at Ejing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun sent Ran Min to Longcheng and beheaded him on Mount Ejing.

sentences.zh: 山左右七里草木悉枯，蝗蟲大起，五月不雨，至於十二月。

translations.literal: For seven li left and right of the mountain all grass and trees withered utterly; locusts arose in great numbers; from the fifth month it did not rain until the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: For seven li around the hill every tree and blade withered; locusts blotted the sky; not a drop fell from the fifth month to the twelfth.

sentences.zh: 俊遣使者祀之，諡曰武悼天王，其日大雪。

translations.literal: Jun sent envoys to sacrifice to him, posthumously titled Martial Lamented Heavenly King; that day great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun offered sacrifice and titled him Martial Lament Heavenly King; snow fell that same day.

sentences.zh: 是歲永和八年也。

translations.literal: That year was the eighth year of Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: It was the eighth year of the Yonghe era.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Historian's appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫拯溺救焚，帝王之師也；

translations.literal: The historians say: To save the drowning and rescue from fire is the way of emperors and kings;
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: To snatch the drowning from the flood and the doomed from the flames is the mark of a true king's host;

sentences.zh: 窮凶騁暴，戎狄之舉也。

translations.literal: to exhaust cruelty and unleash violence is the conduct of the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: to indulge every cruelty and ride every storm of violence is the way of the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 蠢茲雜種，自古為虞，限以塞垣，猶懼侵軼，況乃入居中壤，窺我王政，乘弛紊之機，睹危亡之隙，而莫不嘯群鳴鏑，汨亂天常者乎！

translations.literal: Stupid are these mixed breeds; from antiquity they have been a peril; bounded by the barrier wall, we still fear their raids—how much more when they enter and dwell in the central plain, spy on our royal governance, seize the moment of slack disorder, watch the cracks of peril and destruction, and none fail to howl in packs and scream with arrows, throwing heaven's constant into chaos!
translations.idiomatic: These mongrel hordes have been a frontier worry since antiquity; penned beyond the wall they still raid—how much worse when they squat in the heartland, eye our institutions, strike whenever order frays, and every pack howls and every quiver sings while heaven's order is trampled!

sentences.zh: 石勒出自羌渠，見奇丑類。

translations.literal: Shi Le came from the Qiang Qu channel and was deemed a marvel among the ugly tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rose from the Qiangqu tribes and seemed a prodigy among savage stock.

sentences.zh: 聞鞞上党，季子鑒其非凡；

translations.literal: When the drum sounded in Shangdang, Jizi discerned his extraordinariness;
translations.idiomatic: When his drum echoed in Shangdang, Ji Zi knew he was no common man;

sentences.zh: 倚嘯洛城，夷甫識其為亂。

translations.literal: leaning and whistling in Luoyang, Yifu recognized him as the coming rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: when he lounged whistling in Luoyang, Wang Yan saw the makings of revolt.

sentences.zh: 及惠皇失統，宇內崩離，遂乃招聚蟻徒，乘間煽禍，虔劉我都邑，翦害我黎元。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui lost control and all within the cosmos collapsed and parted, thereupon he gathered ant-like followers, seized the chance to fan disaster, slaughtered our capital cities, and mowed down our black-haired commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Hui lost the reins and the realm split apart, he rallied a swarm of followers, fanned every crisis, gutted our capitals, and mowed down our people.

sentences.zh: 朝市淪胥，若沈航於鯨浪；

translations.literal: The court and market sank together, like sinking a boat in whale waves;
translations.idiomatic: Capitals and markets went under like boats swallowed in a leviathan's swell;

sentences.zh: 王公顛仆，譬游魂于龍漠。

translations.literal: princes and dukes tumbled, like wandering souls in the dragon desert.
translations.idiomatic: princes and dukes fell like lost souls on the dragon sands.

sentences.zh: 豈天厭晉德而假茲妖孽者歟！

translations.literal: Could it be that Heaven loathed Jin's virtue and lent these portents!
translations.idiomatic: Had Heaven tired of Jin's virtue and lent these monsters their hour!

sentences.zh: 觀其對敵臨危，運籌賈勇，奇謨間發，猛氣橫飛。

translations.literal: Observe him facing the enemy on the brink, laying plans and summoning courage, strange stratagems bursting forth, fierce breath flying across the field.
translations.idiomatic: Watch him at the crisis: schemes flashed, courage surged, stratagems sparked, and fury swept the line.

sentences.zh: 遠嗤魏武，則風情慷慨；

translations.literal: Far off he mocked Wei Wu, and his manner was stirring and generous;
translations.idiomatic: From afar he mocked Cao Cao with the bravado of legend;

sentences.zh: 近答劉琨，則音詞倜儻。

translations.literal: Nearer he answered Liu Kun, and his words were free and bold.
translations.idiomatic: face to face with Liu Kun his answers rang with reckless wit.

sentences.zh: 焚元超於苦縣，陳其亂政之愆；

translations.literal: He burned Yuanchao at Kuxian, displaying his crime of disordering governance;
translations.idiomatic: He burned Sima Yue at Kuxian to publish the crime of ruining the state;

sentences.zh: 戮彭祖于襄國，數以無君之罪。

translations.literal: he executed Pengzu at Xiangguo, counting his offense of having no lord.
translations.idiomatic: he struck down Shi Zhi at Xiangguo, charging him with lese-majesty.

sentences.zh: 於是跨躡燕、趙，併吞韓、魏，杖奇材而竊徽號，擁舊都而抗王室，褫毯裘，襲冠帶，釋介胄，開庠序，鄰敵懼威而獻款，絕域承風而納貢，則古之為國，曷以加諸！

translations.literal: Thereupon he strode over Yan and Zhao, swallowed Han and Wei together, leaned on strange talent to steal august titles, hugged the old capitals to resist the royal house, stripped felt and furs, donned caps and sashes, doffed armor, opened schools—border foes feared his might and offered tribute, distant lands caught his wind and sent gifts—how could the ancient founding of states surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: Then he straddled Yan and Zhao, swallowed Han and Wei, leaned on genius to steal the mandate, clutched the old capitals against the throne, traded furs for court dress, armor for schools, until neighbors bought peace with tribute and distant lands sent gifts—what ancient founding outshone that!

sentences.zh: 雖曰凶殘，亦一時傑也。

translations.literal: Although called fierce and cruel, he was still a hero of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel he was called, yet a champion of his age.

sentences.zh: 而托授非所，貽厥無謀，身隕嗣滅，業歸攜養，斯乃知人之暗焉。

translations.literal: Yet he entrusted the succession to the wrong hands, left heirs without counsel, himself perished and posterity was extinguished, the enterprise fell to a fostered child—this shows how dim was his judgment of men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he picked the wrong heir, planned nothing for his sons, died and saw his line snuffed while the work passed to a fosterling—proof how blind he was to men.

sentences.zh: 季龍心昧德義，幼而輕險，假豹姿於羊質，騁梟心於狼性，始懷怨懟，終行篡奪。

translations.literal: Jilong's heart was dark to virtue and duty; from youth he was frivolous and perilous; he borrowed a leopard's posture in a sheep's body and gave rein to an owl heart in a wolf's nature; at first he nursed resentment, in the end he carried out usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong knew neither virtue nor duty; even young he was reckless and dangerous—a leopard's pelt on a sheep, an owl's heart in a wolf; nursed grudges, then seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是窮驕極侈，勞役繁興，畚鍤相尋，干戈不息，刑政嚴酷，動見誅夷，惵惵遺黎，求哀無地，戎狄殘獷，斯為甚乎！

translations.literal: Thereupon he exhausted pride and reached utmost extravagance; corvée and labor rose endlessly; shovels and picks followed one another; shields and spears never rested; punishments and government were harsh and cruel; movement meant execution and slaughter; the trembling surviving commoners had nowhere to beg mercy—among the savagery of Rong and Di, was this not the worst!
translations.idiomatic: Then came boundless pride and waste, endless labor gangs, pick and spade without pause, spear and shield never still, savage law so that motion meant death, and the shivering people nowhere to cry for mercy—among all barbarian cruelty, none surpassed this!

sentences.zh: 既而父子猜嫌，兄弟仇隙，自相屠膾，取笑天下。

translations.literal: Then father and son grew mutually suspicious, brothers bore enmity, slaughtered one another, and became the laughingstock of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Father doubted son, brother hated brother, they carved one another up and made the realm laugh.

sentences.zh: 墳土未燥，禍亂薦臻，釁起于張豺，族傾于冉閔，積惡致滅，有天道哉！

translations.literal: The tomb earth was not yet dry when disasters piled up; rancor rose with Zhang Chai and the clan toppled with Ran Min—accumulated evil brought extinction; does this not show heaven's way!
translations.idiomatic: The clay on their tombs was still damp when ruin piled in—Zhang Chai's grudge, Ran Min's blade, the house fell; piled evil draws heaven's answer!

sentences.zh: 夫從逆則凶，事符影響；

translations.literal: To follow rebellion is ill-omened; the event matches shadow and echo;
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion brings ruin as surely as shadow matches form;

sentences.zh: 為咎必應，理若迴圈。

translations.literal: doing wrong must meet response; the principle is like turning a wheel.
translations.idiomatic: crime calls back answer like a wheel returning on itself.

sentences.zh: 世龍之殪晉人，既窮其酷；

translations.literal: Shilong's slaughter of Jin people already exhausted cruelty;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's slaughter of Jin subjects plumbed every cruelty;

sentences.zh: 永曾之誅羯士，亦殲其類。

translations.literal: Yongzeng's execution of Jie warriors likewise exterminated their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Yongzeng's extirpation of the Jie matched them in ferocity.

sentences.zh: 無德不報，斯之謂乎！

translations.literal: Without virtue there is no repayment not made—does this not speak to it!
translations.idiomatic: No deed lacks its reckoning—so speaks the way of payback!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：中朝不競，蠻狄爭衡。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The central court did not contend; Man and Di strove for mastery.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict runs: When the central court faltered, barbarians wrestled for the helm.

sentences.zh: 塵飛五嶽，霧晻三精。

translations.literal: Dust flew over the five marchmounts; mist dimmed the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Dust veiled the five peaks; mist swallowed sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 狡焉石氏，怙亂窮兵。

translations.literal: Crafty was the Shi clan, relying on turmoil to exhaust the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi house, cunning and cruel, fed on chaos and endless war.

sentences.zh: 流災肆慝，剽邑屠城。

translations.literal: They spread calamity and unleashed villainy, raiding towns and slaughtering cities.
translations.idiomatic: They poured disaster abroad, sacked cities, and butchered towns.

sentences.zh: 始自群盜，終假鴻名。

translations.literal: Beginning as a pack of bandits, in the end they borrowed a great name.
translations.idiomatic: Begun as common brigands, they ended clutching a stolen mandate.

sentences.zh: 勿謂凶醜，亦曰時英。

translations.literal: Do not call them only hideous villains—they too were heroes of the hour.
translations.idiomatic: Call them fiends if you will—they were still titans of their moment.

sentences.zh: 季龍篡奪，淫虐播聲。

translations.literal: Jilong usurped and seized, and the sound of debauchery and cruelty spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong usurped the throne and his name reeked of lust and slaughter.

sentences.zh: 身喪國泯，其由禍盈。

translations.literal: His body lost and the state annihilated—such was the cup of calamity brimming over.
translations.idiomatic: He died, his state vanished—so runs the tale of a brimming cup of woe.
